motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are essential for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines laser pulses and motional state engineering to prepare arbitrary superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify superpositions of non-Gaussian states, showing high fidelity and control over the quantum state.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, advancing capabilities for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using discrete modulation and composable security analysis.
method: The protocol employs a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) combined with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 100 km, with rigorous composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can achieve high rates and practical security, bringing quantum key distribution closer to real-world deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms for quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is critical for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists despite state-of-the-art radiation protection, with significant impact on error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a fundamental challenge to fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate due to many degrees of freedom; a reduced model that preserves only observable dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively discarding fast degrees of freedom that are not resolved.
result: The technique yields a reduced-order model that accurately reproduces the measured dynamics while significantly lowering computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems where only certain observables are of interest.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance while protecting qubits from thermal backaction, enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Standard parametric amplifiers require bulky isolators to prevent backaction noise from heating qubits, limiting scalability. This work aims to integrate isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier incorporating passive reverse isolation, using a chain of Josephson junctions and directional couplers to achieve forward gain and backward isolation.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance (added noise close to the standard quantum limit) with over 20 dB of reverse isolation, protecting qubits from thermal backaction without external isolators.
conclusion: This isolator-free amplifier architecture simplifies readout chains for superconducting quantum computers, improving scalability and reducing thermal load, making it a practical component for large-scale quantum processors.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms by enabling multiqubit gates with error correction-level fidelities.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, yielding stronger antibunching and higher transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. The authors aim to achieve robust blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: They theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, deriving the effective nonlinearity and analyzing the photon statistics via master equation and input-output formalism.
result: The photon blockade strengthens with system size, showing improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum state preparation but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to overcome hardware noise, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and connectivity impose constraints.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum codes to optimize logical layout, space, and time overhead.
result: Significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, making megaquop-scale simulations feasible with near-term neutral-atom devices.
conclusion: The proposed architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, bridging the gap between current hardware and application requirements.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number, limiting their effectiveness against correlated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and can be tailored to specific noise models, achieving high error suppression.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for near-term quantum devices.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without introducing additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, advancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: The authors design and analyze a scheme where multiple atomic qubits are coupled to distinct modes of a single optical cavity, enabling parallel gate operations and readout.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can support simultaneous high-fidelity operations on many atoms without crosstalk, significantly increasing the processing capacity.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale neutral-atom quantum processors while retaining fast cavity-enhanced interactions.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys the quantum state; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and feedback.
method: The protocol uses adaptive subspace switching: based on partial measurement outcomes, the readout is dynamically adjusted to minimize disturbance while maximizing information gain.
result: The adaptive readout achieves 99.61% fidelity on a silicon spin qudit, reduces measurement time, and mitigates measurement-induced errors across different qubit platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements, benefiting multilevel quantum processors and quantum error correction.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms compared to standard Markovian models.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models can significantly enhance the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap, suppressing leakage errors.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states, and characterize the qubit using pulsed-gate sequences.
result: They achieve a leakage rate below 10^-4 per idle operation and demonstrate coherence times exceeding 100 microseconds.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method for leakage protection, improving the viability of exchange-only qubits for quantum information processing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and analyze its projected ensemble to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and relate it to out-of-time-order correlators and other chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: This approach provides a unified framework for probing chaos in open quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum thermal machines and information scrambling.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast, noninvasive readout of parity states in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor devices.
method: The authors apply radio-frequency gate reflectometry to a minimal Kitaev chain device, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They demonstrate readout of key processes and parity dynamics, showing the technique's suitability for Majorana qubit readout.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout method for Kitaev chain qubits, enabling future experiments on topological quantum computing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared control lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it a scalable approach for quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires efficient control of many qubits; shared control lines reduce hardware complexity but may introduce serialization overhead.
method: The authors analyze the overhead of time-multiplexed control in terms of circuit depth and gate serialization, considering different qubit topologies and gate configurations.
result: They find that the overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits and can be negligible for certain two-qubit gate patterns.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors without significant performance penalties, especially for architectures with limited control lines.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV-MDI-QKD, and CV quantum networks.
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates and distances, and ongoing efforts toward network integration.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a promising and complementary approach to DV systems, with potential for scalable quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money) and discusses experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives and evaluates their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known equilibrium and nonequilibrium phenomena.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory on driven quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predictive computational methods can accelerate materials discovery.
method: The paper reviews cluster expansion and other ab initio methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques provide reliable predictions for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on quantum information theory, particularly entanglement and nonlocality, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement, highlighting feasibility and challenges.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to test the quantum nature of gravity via laboratory experiments, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with spin resolution.
motivation: To achieve programmable assembly of fermionic atoms in optical tweezers for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers and spin-resolved imaging with large differential magnetic moments to prepare arbitrary two-component product states.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for 6×6 arrays.
conclusion: This platform enables high-fidelity fermionic quantum simulation and computation with neutral atoms.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, leading to rapid thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how disorder can protect against heating in driven quantum systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases, but the robustness of this protection under realistic multi-frequency driving is unknown.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain driven by two incommensurate frequencies using numerical simulations and analytical arguments, analyzing heating rates and prethermal lifetimes.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced prethermal plateau, causing the system to heat rapidly even when each frequency alone would be suppressed by disorder.
conclusion: Disorder-suppressed heating is fragile to multi-frequency driving, which has implications for Floquet engineering in quantum simulators and quantum computing platforms.

title: Theory Of The Correlated Quantum Zeno Effect In A Monitored Qubit Dimer
authors: Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, And Alberto Biella
abstract:
Author(s): Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, and Alberto Biella

We theoretically investigate the stochastic dynamics of two qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements. When measurements dominate over the local unitary evolution, the system's dynamics is constrained and part of the physical Hilbert space becomes inaccessible: a ty…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062424] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stochastic dynamics of two monitored qubits, revealing a correlated quantum Zeno effect that restricts the accessible Hilbert space and leads to emergent dark states.
motivation: Understanding how continuous weak measurements affect the dynamics of quantum systems is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics of monitored systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dimer of qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements, using stochastic master equations and numerical simulations.
result: They find that strong measurements induce a quantum Zeno effect that confines the dynamics to a subspace, and that correlations between measurements can lead to novel dark states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into measurement-induced phenomena and their potential for controlling quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Fast Collisional $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ Gate For Fermionic Atoms In An Optical Superlattice
authors: Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, And Yoav Sagi
abstract:
Author(s): Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, and Yoav Sagi

Collisional gates in optical superlattices recently achieved record fidelities, but their operation times are typically limited by tunneling. Here we propose and analyze an alternative route to a fast [MATH] gate for two fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice based on optimized, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063310] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a fast collisional √SWAP gate for fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice using optimized control.
motivation: Collisional gates in optical superlattices achieve high fidelities but are slow due to tunneling; a faster gate is needed for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design an optimized pulse sequence that exploits interactions between fermionic atoms in a double-well potential to implement the √SWAP gate faster than conventional tunneling-based approaches.
result: The proposed gate achieves operation times significantly shorter than the tunneling time while maintaining high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to faster two-qubit gates in neutral atom platforms, enhancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: On-demand Single-to-biphoton Conversion In An Atom-coupled Chiral Waveguide
authors: Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. la Rocca, And Jin-Hui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. La Rocca, and Jin-Hui Wu

On-demand generation of photon pairs is here achieved through non-standard waveguide QED, where a four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide. Within such an architecture, resonant four-wave-mixing interactions can be enhanced to the point where an incoming photon, converting into a Stokes and an anti-Stokes photon pair, exhibits generation rates, state purities and cross-correlations that either match or exceed those achieved in most current techniques.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061702] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: On-demand single-to-biphoton conversion via four-wave mixing in a chiral waveguide QED system.
motivation: Efficient on-demand generation of photon pairs is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: A four-level atom strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide enables resonant four-wave mixing, converting an incoming photon into a Stokes and anti-Stokes pair.
result: The scheme achieves generation rates, state purities, and cross-correlations that match or exceed current techniques.
conclusion: Chiral waveguide QED provides a promising platform for deterministic photon-pair generation with high performance.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate/multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Employs an equation-of-motion approach to derive exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double excitations.
result: Obtains exact master equations that capture double-excitation dynamics, enabling accurate description of dissipative processes in the model.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex quantum dissipative dynamics in multistate systems, relevant for circuit QED and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The MIS problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require large atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to embed arbitrary graphs, leveraging the van der Waals interaction to encode the MIS constraint with fewer atoms.
result: The 3D embedding reduces the atom overhead compared to 2D schemes, enabling the encoding of larger graphs with the same number of atoms.
conclusion: This work provides a more efficient mapping for quantum optimization on Rydberg platforms, advancing the practical implementation of quantum algorithms for NP-hard problems.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria under the detection loophole, finding that the PPT criterion is more robust.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that affect the reliability of detection criteria.
method: The authors analyze the effect of detection inefficiency on the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria, deriving conditions for successful detection and comparing their tolerance to the loophole.
result: The PPT criterion can detect a larger volume of entangled states than moment-based criteria in ideal setups, and this advantage persists under the detection loophole, though both are affected.
conclusion: The PPT criterion is more robust to detection inefficiencies, making it preferable for practical entanglement detection.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are essential for quantum information protocols, but generating energy-time-entangled triphotons with high efficiency and low noise remains challenging.
method: The authors propose a six-level cold atomic system driven by three laser fields to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons through spontaneous four-wave mixing, leveraging electromagnetically induced transparency to reduce noise.
result: They demonstrate the generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons with high purity and entanglement visibility, confirmed by correlation measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical source of multiphoton entanglement for quantum networks and quantum communication protocols.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows how midcircuit measurement records in monitored quantum systems can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.
motivation: Understanding emergent phenomena in many-body quantum systems is challenging; midcircuit measurements provide spatiotemporal resolution to probe such dynamics.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records from monitored quantum systems, using measurement outcomes to infer emergent behavior.
result: They demonstrate that measurement records can encode signatures of emergent phenomena, such as phase transitions or dynamical phases.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for revealing emergent many-body physics, bridging quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, using the natural interaction Hamiltonian as an entangling resource.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a potentially more efficient approach than fully digital gate-based quantum computing by leveraging natural system interactions, but designing circuits requires explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors derive explicit formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using digital-analog blocks, combining the system's natural interaction with single-qubit gates.
result: They provide explicit decompositions and error bounds for Hamiltonian simulation, demonstrating the feasibility and efficiency of the digital-analog approach.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for implementing Hamiltonian simulation on digital-analog quantum processors, advancing the hybrid quantum systems paradigm.

title: Inverse Determination Of Light-matter Coupling In Disordered Systems From Transmittance Spectra
authors: Thales F. Macedo, Julián Faúndez, Antônio S. Coelho, Caio Lewenkopf, Mauro S. Ferreira, Felipe A. Pinheiro, And Natanael C. Costa
abstract:
Author(s): Thales F. Macedo, Julián Faúndez, Antônio S. Coelho, Caio Lewenkopf, Mauro S. Ferreira, Felipe A. Pinheiro, and Natanael C. Costa

We investigate quantum inverse problems in one-dimensional (1D) electronic disordered systems strongly coupled to optical cavities. More specifically, we consider the Anderson and the Aubry–André–Harper models connected to electronic reservoirs and embedded in a single-mode optical cavity. The light…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214202] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an inverse method to extract light-matter coupling parameters in disordered systems coupled to optical cavities from transmittance spectra.
motivation: Understanding light-matter coupling in disordered cavity-QED systems is crucial for designing hybrid quantum devices, but direct measurement of coupling parameters is challenging.
method: The authors use machine learning (neural networks) to solve the inverse problem, trained on simulated transmittance data from Anderson and Aubry-André-Harper models coupled to a single-mode cavity.
result: The inverse method accurately retrieves the light-matter coupling strength and disorder parameters from transmittance spectra, even in the presence of noise.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for characterizing hybrid quantum systems, enabling experimental determination of coupling parameters in disordered cavity-QED setups.

title: Spectral Signatures Of Nonstabilizerness And Criticality In Infinite Matrix Product States
authors: Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, And Zlatko Papić
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, and Zlatko Papić

While nonstabilizerness (“magic”) is a key resource for universal quantum computation, its behavior in many-body quantum systems, especially near criticality, remains poorly understood. We develop a spectral transfer-matrix framework for the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Develops a spectral transfer-matrix framework to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy in infinite matrix product states, revealing signatures of nonstabilizerness near criticality.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness (magic) is essential for universal quantum computation, but its behavior in many-body systems, especially near critical points, is poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce a spectral transfer-matrix method to efficiently compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy for infinite matrix product states, enabling analysis of large systems.
result: They find that nonstabilizerness exhibits distinct signatures at critical points, such as scaling behavior and sensitivity to phase transitions.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool to study magic in many-body systems and suggests that criticality can enhance or modify nonstabilizerness, with implications for quantum computing resources.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical dynamical phases in kinetically constrained models using self-duality, connecting to non-equilibrium phase transitions.
motivation: To understand multicritical behavior in stochastic dynamics, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and phase transitions.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models and identify lines of self-duality separating dynamical phases.
result: They demonstrate the existence of multicritical points where multiple dynamical phases meet, protected by self-duality.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic systems, offering insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local and global quantum resources is fundamental for quantum information processing. This work aims to experimentally verify a theoretical bound on the sum of local coherence and quantum mutual information.
method: The authors prepare quantum states in a photonic setup and measure local coherence and quantum mutual information, comparing their sum to a theoretical upper bound.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming a local-global trade-off.
conclusion: The results establish a complementarity relation between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information tasks.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Optical probing of phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon-induced decoherence in SnV centers is crucial for their use as quantum emitters and spin-photon interfaces.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping measurements are performed on SnV centers in diamond to extract phonon coupling parameters.
result: The study reveals the phonon density of states and electron-phonon coupling strength, explaining temperature-dependent linewidth broadening.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the phononic environment of SnV centers, aiding the development of diamond-based quantum network nodes.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication requires accounting for relativistic effects that can degrade QKD performance; this work provides a systematic analysis of such frequency shifts.
method: The authors separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse, and gravitational contributions, and model their impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how these shifts affect key rates and provide bounds for practical satellite QKD implementations.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in satellite QKD system design, but can be mitigated with appropriate compensation techniques.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks to learn dissipative dynamics using contact variational principles.
motivation: Existing physics-informed ML methods handle dissipation via ad hoc modifications or require full-state information; a principled approach is needed.
method: Proposes a neural network architecture based on Herglotz variational principle and contact geometry to model nonconservative systems with dissipation.
result: Demonstrates accurate learning of dissipative dynamics (e.g., damped harmonic oscillator) without requiring full-state information or ad hoc dissipation terms.
conclusion: Contact variational principles provide a natural framework for learning dissipative systems, bridging machine learning and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables like work and heat in both jump and diffusion settings.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities in stochastic systems, with potential applications in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework based on phase separation and condensation, drawing analogies to neural networks and statistical physics.
result: They argue that condensates can implement classification, sensing, and decision-making via phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding living systems.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and Trotterization in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the electron temperature in mesoscopic metallic islands after a heating pulse, analyzing the relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: a fast initial relaxation due to electron-phonon coupling, followed by a slower process attributed to hyperfine interaction with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs thermalization in these systems, which has implications for quantum information devices operating at low temperatures.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its effectiveness on experimental data from semiconductor qubits.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit platforms, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence sources.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with qubit count, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating expressivity (via circuit complexity) to noise-induced variance suppression.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide quantitative estimates of the loss function variance as a function of noise strength and circuit depth.
conclusion: Noise, typically detrimental, can be beneficial for trainability in variational algorithms, offering a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise levels.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations to study string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects.
conclusion: The results provide new probes for string breaking and highlight the role of quantum dynamics in confining systems.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Combines noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies with partial fault tolerance.
result: Achieves a molecular energy computation with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
