result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: This work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different approaches and aids in advancing simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can simplify certain gates and reduce resource overhead, motivating a survey of their roles.
method: The paper reviews theoretical embeddings of qudits into qubit systems, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of multiqubit gates, reducing circuit depth and potentially improving fidelity, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, by leveraging higher-dimensional Hilbert spaces to simplify algorithms.

title: Layer Codes As Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories
authors: Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, And Eugene Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, and Eugene Tang

We investigate layer codes, a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieves optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, as candidates for self-correcting quantum memories. First, we introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210601] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Layer codes are 3D stabilizer codes with optimal scaling and energy barrier, studied as partially self-correcting quantum memories.
motivation: To find quantum memories that can protect information without active error correction, leveraging self-correcting properties.
method: Introduces two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees under local stochastic noise, and analyzes energy barriers and memory lifetime.
result: Layer codes achieve optimal code parameters and energy barrier scaling, but are only partially self-correcting with limited memory lifetime.
conclusion: Layer codes improve upon previous 3D codes but do not achieve full self-correction; further work needed for practical quantum memories.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear auxiliary term in the quantum Rabi model to globalize critical quantum metrology, enhancing sensitivity across parameter regimes.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is limited to a local regime; the authors aim to extend its applicability globally.
method: They introduce an auxiliary nonlinear term to the quantum Rabi model and analyze the resulting dynamics and critical behavior.
result: The nonlinear term enables global critical quantum metrology with improved sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed modification broadens the scope of critical quantum metrology in light-matter systems.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve gradient estimation in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Efficient and reliable gradient estimation is a central challenge for QAOA and variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ era.
method: The authors analyze QAOA gradients in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that relate gradient components to the Hamiltonian spectrum and using filtering techniques to reduce noise.
result: They demonstrate that frequency-domain gradient estimators can achieve lower variance and improved convergence compared to standard finite-difference methods.
conclusion: The frequency-domain approach provides a provably reliable gradient estimation method for QAOA, potentially enhancing performance of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hyperentanglement-based quantum reservoir computing framework that uses multiple degrees of freedom of photons to enhance computational capacity.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is promising for temporal tasks, but standard QRC with single-degree-of-freedom entanglement may have limited expressivity. Hyperentanglement offers a way to increase the reservoir's effective dimension and performance.
method: The authors design a QRC architecture where the reservoir consists of hyperentangled photon pairs (e.g., polarization and orbital angular momentum). Input encoding, reservoir dynamics, and readout are implemented via linear optics and projective measurements.
result: Numerical simulations show that hyperentanglement-based QRC outperforms standard QRC on benchmark tasks (e.g., memory capacity, nonlinear transformation) and achieves higher accuracy with fewer reservoir nodes.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement is a viable resource for enhancing QRC performance, potentially leading to more efficient quantum machine learning implementations.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. McFarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, and Peter J. Love

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. We perform simulations to compare the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit [MATH] rotation and discrete SK dec…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, comparing trace distances between ideal and discretized rotations.
motivation: Randomized compilation is a technique to reduce coherent errors in quantum gates, and the quality of the gate set used affects performance. The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm provides a method to approximate arbitrary single-qubit gates with a finite universal gate set.
method: The authors perform simulations of the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm to generate ensembles of one-qubit rotations and compute the trace distance between the ideal quantum state and the state obtained after applying the discretized rotation from the SK decomposition.
result: The simulations quantify the trade-off between approximation accuracy (trace distance) and the number of gates in the decomposition, providing insights into the effectiveness of SK-generated ensembles for randomized compilation.
conclusion: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm can produce gate sets suitable for randomized compilation, but the overhead in gate count may limit practical applicability for near-term quantum devices.

title: Robust Applicability Of Continuous Dynamical Decoupling To Decoherence Reduction In Longitudinal And Transverse-noise Settings: The Role Of Anisotropy
authors: S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, And J. Plata
abstract:
Author(s): S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, and J. Plata

We analytically evaluate the efficiency of continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to curb decoherence in generic qubit setups where diverse sources of noise can be present. Previous theoretical approaches to CDD have mainly focused on its potential to cope with longitudinal fluctuations. Here, the ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062412] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical evaluation of continuous dynamical decoupling for decoherence reduction in qubit setups with both longitudinal and transverse noise, highlighting the role of noise anisotropy.
motivation: Previous CDD studies focused on longitudinal noise; this work extends to transverse noise and anisotropic settings to assess robustness.
method: Analytical derivation of decoherence suppression efficiency under CDD for generic qubit models with arbitrary noise spectra.
result: CDD effectively reduces decoherence in both longitudinal and transverse noise, but its performance depends on noise anisotropy and spectral properties.
conclusion: CDD is a robust decoherence mitigation technique applicable to a wide range of noise environments, with anisotropy playing a key role.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, and Leonardo Mazza

We show that in classical spin systems, the precise nature of the late-time hydrodynamic tails of the autocorrelation functions of a generic observable is determined by (i) the dynamical critical exponent and (ii) the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the corresponding observable. We provide n…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems are determined by dynamical critical exponent and equilibrium thermodynamic properties, with a quantum extension.
motivation: Understanding late-time dynamics and hydrodynamic behavior in spin systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for autocorrelation functions using hydrodynamic theory and test them on classical and quantum spin chains.
result: They find that the exponent of the hydrodynamic tail depends on the dynamical critical exponent and the thermodynamic susceptibility of the observable.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for hydrodynamic tails in both classical and quantum spin systems, linking dynamics to equilibrium properties.

title: Hyperuniformity In Active Fluids Reshapes Nucleation And Capillary-wave Dynamics
authors: Raphaël Maire
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Maire

Nucleation in active and driven fluids often resembles equilibrium behavior, but a departure occurs when large-scale density fluctuations are strongly suppressed. In this work, it is demonstrated that droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential instead of the classical reversible work of formation.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064103] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nucleation in active hyperuniform fluids, showing that droplet formation is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential rather than classical reversible work.
motivation: Understanding nucleation in active fluids is important for nonequilibrium thermodynamics, but hyperuniformity is a niche topic not directly aligned with core interests.
method: Theoretical analysis using a quasipotential approach for nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids.
result: Droplet nucleation in hyperuniform active fluids is controlled by a nonequilibrium quasipotential, deviating from classical nucleation theory.
conclusion: Hyperuniformity reshapes nucleation dynamics, but the work is more about soft matter physics than quantum information thermodynamics.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
authors: D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, And S. J. Thomson
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, and S. J. Thomson

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems using imaginary time spectral transforms and tensor networks.
motivation: Preparing excited states is important for understanding quantum systems, but existing methods are often computationally expensive or require matrix inversion.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion, implemented via tensor-network simulations.
result: Demonstrated on disordered spin chains, showing accurate preparation of excited eigenstates.
conclusion: The method is compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations and offers a practical approach for excited-state preparation.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize optical non-Gaussian state generation, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to improve scalability.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond stellar rank and develop a systematic optimization framework for optical state generation.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for scalable quantum light sources, advancing optical quantum computing and networking.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a two-dimensional electron gas in a Landau level, combined with thermodynamic analysis.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom is observed, and sensitivity is achieved to constrain topological entropy.
conclusion: The approach can isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, advancing the study of topological order.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; the paper aims to reduce overhead using quantum LDPC codes.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate, and demonstrates their use in generating CCZ magic states via constant-depth circuits.
result: Tricycle codes achieve efficient magic state generation with improved noise tolerance compared to existing schemes, analyzed via finite block-length simulations.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to reduce magic state distillation overhead, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing. The tutorial aims to provide a pedagogical introduction to this approach.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including Fisher information, scaling analysis, and protocols for exploiting criticality.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum sensors can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling and discusses experimental platforms such as trapped ions and superconducting circuits.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for high-precision metrology, but practical challenges like decoherence and finite-size effects must be addressed.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a moment-matching technique to construct a unitary dilation on a 1D lattice, enabling efficient simulation of linear differential equations.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation by exploiting commuting structures in quantum circuits.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates (T-count) is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement. The paper aims to find a systematic way to reduce T-count beyond existing methods.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting multiple Pauli products through T gates, enabling more efficient circuit rewriting. They apply this to sequential Pauli-based computation, a model where gates are applied sequentially.
result: The proposed relation reduces T-count significantly compared to previous approaches, with theoretical bounds and examples demonstrating improvement.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for T-count reduction, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation, though the practical impact depends on integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to learn and extrapolate dynamics.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian from trajectory data, then predicts observable dynamics and operator growth.
result: The method accurately reproduces dynamics beyond training time and captures operator growth features.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to identify and assess Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and quantifiers for robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, incorporating interactions.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how well Majorana bound states are protected and localized, which is crucial for braiding operations.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to guide experiments toward realizing topological qubits based on Majorana bound states.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing the simulation to be performed with reduced overhead. This technique leverages the structure of logical circuits to simplify the error analysis.
result: The proposed simulation approach is shown to be scalable and efficient for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling classical verification of these protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for simulating magic state preparation, which is important for benchmarking and verifying fault-tolerant quantum computing schemes.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes by carefully designing the measurement sequence and using the code's structure.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining the code's distance and other properties, and it is compatible with a wide class of LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes, a key step toward scalable quantum architectures.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to fermionic systems, specifically Majorana-based qubits, and constructs high-rate codes and fault-tolerant operations.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana-based qubits requires error correction tailored to fermionic statistics, which differ from standard qubit codes.
method: The authors generalize stabilizer formalism to fermionic systems, design fault-tolerant gates and measurements, and construct high-rate quantum codes using Majorana modes.
result: They demonstrate that fault-tolerant operations are possible with Majorana-based codes and achieve high encoding rates.
conclusion: Majorana-based quantum codes can support fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path for topological quantum computing.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: Uses Pauli propagation to track the evolution of Pauli operators under noisy quantum circuits, deriving conditions for efficient classical simulation.
result: Arbitrary local noise enables efficient classical simulation of typical quantum circuits, with the simulation cost scaling polynomially in the number of qubits.
conclusion: Noise can be a resource for classical simulability, which has implications for quantum advantage experiments and error mitigation.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to identify the most squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling near-constant hardware scaling for photonic processors.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources; the authors aim to compress this to near-constant scaling by focusing on the most relevant squeezed modes.
method: They use a variational approach to find the supermodes with the strongest squeezing, effectively reducing the number of required modes for processing.
result: The method achieves a dramatic reduction in hardware footprint, from quadratic to near-constant scaling, while maintaining processing fidelity.
conclusion: Variational selection of squeezed supermodes offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic processing, with implications for quantum information processing and sensing.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires high error thresholds and low overhead, but existing codes like surface codes have high overhead. Radial codes aim to improve these metrics.
method: The authors introduce radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes with tunable parameters, and analyze their error correction capabilities using numerical simulations.
result: Radial codes achieve high thresholds, low overhead, and single-shot decoding, making them promising for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for practical fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing performance and resource requirements.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Discusses mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, carrier dynamics, and emergence of metastable orders like superconductivity.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations as due to violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are widely assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements in various fields exceed them, prompting a need to understand why and how to exploit such behavior.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that apparent violations arise from non-equilibrium conditions, inhomogeneities, or other departures from the assumptions of the bounds, and shows how these can be used to engineer materials with enhanced properties.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds allows for the design of materials that surpass conventional limits, with implications for metamaterials and other advanced materials.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but the paper focuses on a specific class of states and decoherence dynamics rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects.
method: The authors use phase-space methods and Wigner function negativity to quantify decoherence for compass states and generalize to other states.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale of the state, with finer structures decohering faster.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decoherence dynamics but does not directly advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Chirped-pulse Engineering For Robust Control Of Single-molecule Orientation In A Cavity
authors: Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, And Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, and Chuan-Cun Shu

We present a theoretical investigation of coherent control over the orientation of an individual molecule strongly coupled with a cavity using chirped-pulse driving. Specifically, we explore the dynamics of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules under the influence of two chirped pulses with different spe…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063106] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates coherent control of single-molecule orientation in a cavity using chirped pulses.
motivation: To achieve robust orientation control of molecules strongly coupled to a cavity, which is relevant for quantum information processing and molecular dynamics.
method: The authors model the dynamics of OCS molecules in a cavity under two chirped pulses with different speeds, using a theoretical framework based on the Jaynes-Cummings model.
result: They demonstrate that chirped-pulse driving can enhance orientation control and robustness against parameter variations.
conclusion: Chirped-pulse engineering offers a promising route for coherent control of molecular orientation in cavity QED systems.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Investigates PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations on a wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol in coupled quantum systems.
motivation: To explore how non-unitary, PT-symmetric dynamics affect the traversability of holography-inspired teleportation, connecting quantum information with non-Hermitian physics.
method: Models a minimal wormhole teleportation protocol with coupled SYK-like systems and introduces a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformation, analyzing the resulting dynamics and teleportation fidelity.
result: The PT-symmetric deformation can enhance or suppress teleportation traversability depending on parameters, showing a transition between effective Hermitian and non-Hermitian regimes.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations offer a new control knob for quantum teleportation protocols, with potential implications for quantum information processing and holographic dualities.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision of Gaussian channel parameters, using quantum metrology tools.
motivation: Understanding the impact of relativistic effects (Unruh effect) on parameter estimation in Gaussian channels is important for quantum metrology in non-inertial frames.
method: The authors model the Unruh effect as a Gaussian channel and compute the quantum Fisher information for estimating channel parameters such as transmissivity and noise.
result: The Unruh effect reduces the estimation precision, and the degradation depends on the acceleration parameter and the channel type.
conclusion: Relativistic motion imposes fundamental limits on quantum metrology with Gaussian states, which must be accounted for in high-precision experiments.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods to attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg processors, but the contribution is primarily in quantum machine learning rather than core quantum information theory.
motivation: To enable graph classification with attributed graphs on quantum hardware, leveraging the native interactions of neutral-atom arrays.
method: The authors embed edge features into atomic positions and use local detuning of a Rydberg Hamiltonian to compute graph kernels, extending the quantum-feature kernel framework.
result: They demonstrate a scheme for attributed-graph kernel implementation on neutral-atom QPUs, with potential advantages for certain graph learning tasks.
conclusion: The work provides a practical quantum machine learning approach but does not advance fundamental quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Tidal Locking In Orbiting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, And Xiaoji Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, and Xiaoji Zhou

Angular momentum coupling manifests widely in diverse physical systems, underpinning the emergent properties and collective dynamics across different scales. The tidal locking, which originates from the synchronization of rotational and orbital motions, has far-reaching impacts in celestial mechanic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies angular momentum coupling and tidal locking in orbiting Bose-Einstein condensates, demonstrating synchronization of rotational and orbital motions.
motivation: Tidal locking is a universal phenomenon in celestial mechanics, but its quantum analog has not been explored. The authors aim to realize quantum tidal locking in a controlled ultracold atom system.
method: They theoretically model two Bose-Einstein condensates in circular orbits, coupled via a harmonic trap, and analyze the dynamics using mean-field theory and quantum master equations.
result: They find that the system exhibits synchronization of the internal rotation with the orbital motion, analogous to classical tidal locking, and that this effect is robust against dissipation.
conclusion: Quantum tidal locking provides a new platform for studying angular momentum coupling and synchronization in quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and simulation.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Photon Drag In A Tunneling-coupled Quantum-dot System
authors: Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, And Zareen A. Khan
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, and Zareen A. Khan

We present a theoretical study of enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag within a four-level quantum-dot setup under the effect of dual interdot tunneling. Using the density-matrix formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field cond…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063709] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of slow-light-enhanced photon drag in a tunneling-coupled quantum-dot system.
motivation: To explore enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag effects using slow light in a quantum-dot system with interdot tunneling.
method: Density-matrix formalism to derive analytical expressions for susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field conditions.
result: Demonstrates significant enhancement of photon drag due to slow light and tunneling coupling.
conclusion: The proposed system offers a platform for controlling light propagation via photon drag, with potential applications in optical switching and sensing.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies localization and scattering of a single photon in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: Understanding photon transport in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum networks and light-matter interfaces, but the focus here is on quasiperiodic order rather than practical networking or transduction.
method: The authors model a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings and analyze the scattering properties and localization of single-photon states using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that increasing quasiperiodic strength leads to a continuum of localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetimes near the resonant frequency, contrasting with the discrete bound states in periodic arrays.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic qubit arrays can host a continuum of long-lived subradiant states, which may be useful for quantum memory or slow-light applications, but the work is primarily a theoretical study of a specific physical system.

title: Geometric Approach To Strongly Correlated Bosons: From $N$-representability To The Generalized Bose-Einstein Condensate Force
authors: Chih-Chun Wang And Christian Schilling
abstract:
Author(s): Chih-Chun Wang and Christian Schilling

Building on recent advances in reduced density matrix theory, we develop a geometric framework for describing strongly correlated lattice bosons. We first establish that translational symmetry, together with a fixed pair interaction, enables an exact functional formulation expressed solely in terms …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224511] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A geometric framework for strongly correlated bosons using reduced density matrix theory and N-representability conditions.
motivation: To develop a functional theory for bosonic systems that avoids the complexity of the full many-body wavefunction.
method: Leverages translational symmetry and fixed pair interactions to formulate an exact functional in terms of the two-particle reduced density matrix.
result: Derives a generalized Bose-Einstein condensate force and provides a geometric interpretation of correlation effects.
conclusion: The framework offers a new perspective on strongly correlated bosons and may enable efficient numerical methods.

title: Unified Statistical Theory Of Heat Conduction In Nonuniform Media
authors: Yi Zeng And Jianjun Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Zeng and Jianjun Dong

Using the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, we derive a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel for heat conduction, defined microscopically as a space-resolved equilibrium heat-flux time-correlation function, that encodes temporal memory, spatial nonlocality, and material heterogeneity on equal…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235204] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel for heat conduction from microscopic equilibrium correlations using the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism.
motivation: To unify temporal memory, spatial nonlocality, and material heterogeneity in heat conduction within a single statistical framework.
method: Uses the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism to derive a space-resolved equilibrium heat-flux time-correlation function as the kernel.
result: Obtains a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel that encodes memory, nonlocality, and heterogeneity on equal footing.
conclusion: Provides a unified statistical theory of heat conduction applicable to nonuniform media.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion induce directed motion and negative mobility in overdamped stochastic systems.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries can generate directed motion and negative mobility in stochastic systems, which is relevant to transport in confined geometries.
method: The authors study overdamped Langevin dynamics with anisotropic diffusion and hard reflecting boundaries, deriving the no-flux condition and analyzing trajectory statistics.
result: They show that boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed motion and can lead to negative mobility.
conclusion: The findings reveal a mechanism for directed transport in confined systems without external bias, with implications for nanoscale devices and biological systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: To understand anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata beyond the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic theory is applied to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: The exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained and shown to be anomalous.
conclusion: Hydrodynamics successfully captures the fluctuation properties of these stochastic systems.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, and to characterize the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is applied.
method: The authors use the trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to build ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition via a transverse magnetic field.
result: They show that each of the 256 elementary cellular automata corresponds to a distinct classical spin model, and they characterize the quantum phase transition for these models.
conclusion: The work provides a new mapping between cellular automata and spin models, offering insights into quantum phase transitions in these constructed systems.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond constant diffusion coefficients and understand defect dynamics in a periodic potential landscape.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a hexagonal colloidal lattice are analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The spatially varying transport coefficients reveal the emergence of a periodic potential for the defects.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of defect motion in a colloidal crystal, relevant to understanding transport in periodic potentials.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions.
conclusion: Fractional derivative models can capture nonlocal effects that break local equilibrium, relevant for nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions In Certain Nonergodic Stochastic Processes
authors: Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, And Tridib Sadhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, and Tridib Sadhu

We present a class of stochastic processes in which the large deviation functions of time-integrated observables exhibit singularities that relate to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories. These illustrative examples include Brownian motion with a death rate or in the presence of an absorbing …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064104] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies dynamical phase transitions in large deviation functions of time-integrated observables for certain nonergodic stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand singularities in large deviation functions that signal dynamical phase transitions in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a class of stochastic processes including Brownian motion with a death rate or absorbing boundaries, and compute large deviation functions analytically or via numerical simulations.
result: They find that the large deviation functions exhibit singularities corresponding to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories, characterized by changes in the optimal path ensemble.
conclusion: The work provides illustrative examples of dynamical phase transitions in nonergodic stochastic processes, contributing to the theory of large deviations and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, showing that the Kondo temperature can be controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and explore how topological bound states can host Kondo physics.
method: Using numerical methods (e.g., DMRG or exact diagonalization) on a one-dimensional interacting SSH chain coupled to a metallic substrate.
result: The Kondo temperature depends on the topological mass parameter, allowing control over the emergent Kondo scale.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a tunable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum devices.

title: Controlled Buildup Of Half-quantized Thermal Conductance In An Engineered Chiral Spin Liquid Platform
authors: Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Nathan Goldman

We study thermal transport along the edge of a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, a platform suitable for quantum-engineered systems. Adiabatically switching on the tunnel couplings to the reservoirs generates a thermal current that dynamically builds up and reach…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023226] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies thermal transport in a chiral spin liquid device coupled to reservoirs, focusing on the buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance.
motivation: To understand thermal transport in engineered quantum systems and explore signatures of topological order via thermal conductance quantization.
method: The authors model a small chiral spin liquid edge coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs and adiabatically switch on tunnel couplings to study the dynamic buildup of thermal current.
result: They find that the thermal conductance builds up to a half-quantized value, reflecting the topological nature of the chiral spin liquid.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a controlled platform for observing half-quantized thermal conductance, relevant for probing topological phases in engineered systems.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectral analysis.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of large matrices is important for quantum many-body physics and quantum computing, but worst-case complexity is high.
method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm that filters eigenvalue clusters and estimates multiplicities using quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial speedup over classical methods for certain spectral properties, particularly when multiplicities are large.
conclusion: The work provides a new quantum tool for spectral analysis, but its direct relevance to the user's core interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics is limited.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods can handle chemical systems and extend to ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful, unified approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System
authors: Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, And Jingyun Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, and Jingyun Fan

Extended, localized, and critical states form the three elementary classes of eigenstates underlying Anderson localization. While phases involving extended and localized states are widely studied, experimental realization of critical phases, particularly those where critical states coexist with othe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of five distinct localization phases in a 1D Floquet system, including critical phases.
motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize critical phases in disordered Floquet systems, which are less explored than extended and localized phases.
method: Using a photonic waveguide array with controlled disorder and periodic driving, measuring wavefunction statistics and transport properties.
result: Five distinct phases are identified: extended, localized, critical, and two mixed phases where critical states coexist with extended or localized states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the richness of localization phenomena in Floquet systems and provides a platform for studying critical phases.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced resource overhead using analytic iterative reconstructions.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources, and quantum machine learning success depends on efficient feature maps.
method: Proposes Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…) to reduce the number of gates and qubits needed.
result: Demonstrates reduced resource overhead while maintaining classification accuracy on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: The method enables more practical quantum machine learning on near-term devices.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of spin and valley dynamics in a monolayer semiconductor using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect, achieving subpicosecond manipulation.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information processing in van der Waals heterostructures.
method: The authors use femtosecond optical pulses to excite and probe spin and valley coherence in a monolayer WSe2 on a ferromagnetic substrate, exploiting the magnetic proximity effect.
result: They observe subpicosecond coherent oscillations of the valley polarization and spin polarization, with control over the phase and amplitude via the magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The anomalous magnetic proximity effect enables ultrafast coherent control of spin and valley degrees of freedom, offering a pathway for valleytronic quantum devices.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan

The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity in α-RuCl3, attributed to chiral Majorana edge modes, but the focus is on condensed matter physics of topological phases rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To confirm the existence of non-Abelian anyons via chiral edge modes in a Kitaev candidate material, addressing reproducibility issues of quantized thermal Hall effect.
method: Geometric engineering of the thermal Hall effect in α-RuCl3 single crystals, measuring thermal Hall conductivity as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: Observation of half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity consistent with chiral Majorana edge modes, with improved reproducibility through sample engineering.
conclusion: The results provide strong evidence for non-Abelian anyons in α-RuCl3, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter physics experiment with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Loss-resistant Bright-seeded Su(1,1) Quantum Interferometer Based On Joint Detection
authors: Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

A quantum interferometer can achieve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit by using the nonclassical properties of the quantum state. The SU(1,1) interferometer, a commonly used quantum interferometer, can be realized by replacing the linear beam splitters in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer wit…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063712] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A loss-resistant SU(1,1) quantum interferometer using bright-seeded joint detection to enhance phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit.
motivation: To overcome the sensitivity degradation due to internal losses in SU(1,1) interferometers, which limits their practical quantum-enhanced metrology performance.
method: The authors propose a bright-seeded SU(1,1) interferometer with joint detection, theoretically analyzing its phase sensitivity under loss using a quantum optics model.
result: The scheme achieves phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit even with significant internal losses, demonstrating loss resistance.
conclusion: The bright-seeded joint detection approach provides a practical way to realize robust quantum-enhanced interferometry.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, and Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition between Floquet and Bloch topological regimes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations, and quasienergy band analysis reveals topological transitions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch topological modes, contributing to the understanding of topological photonics.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical techniques for laser cooling are inefficient for large crystals.
method: The authors develop and apply optimized numerical methods to simulate Doppler laser cooling of 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: They identify optimal cooling parameters that reduce cooling time and improve final temperature, enhancing the performance of quantum sensing protocols.
