conclusion: Optimized Doppler cooling protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals for high-sensitivity quantum sensing.

title: Rabi Oscillations With Close-range Quantum Vortex States
authors: Sam Patrick
abstract:
Author(s): Sam Patrick

Quantum vortices separated by distances much larger than their core size interact via their long-range velocity field. At smaller separations, however, the influence of the core's compressibility strongly influences the vortex dynamics. Using the example of a compact necklace of five vortices, it is…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063309] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Rabi oscillations of quantum vortices in a Bose-Einstein condensate at close range, focusing on core compressibility effects.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics at small separations is important for quantum turbulence and superfluid hydrodynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use a compact necklace of five vortices and analyze their dynamics via numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
result: They find that core compressibility significantly alters the Rabi oscillation frequency and damping compared to point-vortex models.
conclusion: Close-range vortex interactions require models that account for core structure, but the work remains within condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Robust Quantum Control For Bragg Pulse Design In Atom Interferometry
authors: Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, And Malcolm G. Boshier
abstract:
Author(s): Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, and Malcolm G. Boshier

We formulate a robust optimal control algorithm to synthesize minimum-energy pulses that can transfer a cold atom system into various momentum states. The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iterate the control towards a minimum-ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063305] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A robust optimal control algorithm for designing Bragg pulses in atom interferometry, focusing on momentum state transfer.
motivation: To improve the robustness and efficiency of Bragg pulse design for cold atom interferometry, which is sensitive to experimental imperfections.
method: Uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iteratively find minimum-energy control pulses.
result: Demonstrates robust pulse designs that achieve high-fidelity momentum state transfer under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm provides a systematic way to design robust quantum control pulses for atom interferometry applications.

title: Topological Routing In Chern Insulators
authors: Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, And Sean D. Nixon
abstract:
Author(s): Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, and Sean D. Nixon

Chern insulator systems are realizable in numerous physical systems and can support robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy. A routing functionality constructed from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions, using coupled Haldane-type systems is proposed. By adjusting the strength of a magnet…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063510] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a topological routing scheme in Chern insulators using coupled Haldane-type systems for robust nonreciprocal energy transmission.
motivation: To achieve robust routing of energy in photonic or electronic systems by exploiting topological properties of Chern insulators.
method: The authors design a routing structure from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions and adjust the strength of a magnet to control the routing.
result: The system supports robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy, enabling topological routing.
conclusion: Topological routing in Chern insulators is feasible and may have applications in robust energy transport.

title: Intrinsic Quasiparticle Lifetime In Superconducting Aluminum
authors: K. Norowski, M. Foltyn, A. Savin, And M. Zgirski
abstract:
Author(s): K. Norowski, M. Foltyn, A. Savin, and M. Zgirski

We use time-resolved thermometry to monitor the decay of nonequilibrium quasiparticles in superconducting Al in the temperature range from [MATH] to [MATH]. The quasiparticle lifetime at higher temperatures ([MATH]) agrees well …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214512] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Measures quasiparticle lifetime in superconducting aluminum using time-resolved thermometry.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics is important for superconducting qubit coherence, but the paper focuses on material properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved thermometry to monitor decay of nonequilibrium quasiparticles in Al films.
result: Quasiparticle lifetime agrees with theory at higher temperatures but deviates at lower temperatures.
conclusion: Provides experimental data on quasiparticle lifetime, relevant for superconducting device engineering but not directly advancing the user's research directions.

title: Generation Of Chirality And Orbital Magnetization By Stone-Wales-type Lattice Defects In The Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

In this work we extend our study of the effect of certain crystallographic defects on the spin-1/2 Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, focusing on its gapless phase and contrasting with the gapped phase. We identify a Stone-Wales (SW) local defect consisting of a [MATH] bond rotation that preserves Ki…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224419] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales lattice defects on the Kitaev spin liquid, focusing on chirality and orbital magnetization.
motivation: Understanding how crystallographic defects affect the properties of quantum spin liquids is important for characterizing real materials.
method: The authors analyze the Kitaev honeycomb model with Stone-Wales defects using analytical and numerical methods, examining both gapless and gapped phases.
result: They find that Stone-Wales defects generate chirality and orbital magnetization in the Kitaev spin liquid.
conclusion: Lattice defects can induce topological and magnetic responses in Kitaev materials, which may be observable experimentally.

title: Theory Of Relaxation And Its Effects On The Electronic Structure In Twisted Systems
authors: Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, and Cheng-Cheng Liu

Here, the authors present an analytical and physically transparent theory of lattice relaxation in twisted systems. They show how the balance between intralayer elasticity and interlayer adhesion determines the relaxation pattern, and how this pattern can be analytically embedded into moiré electronic Hamiltonians. The work reveals how relaxation reshapes flat bands and shifts topological transitions toward experimentally relevant twist angles.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An analytical theory of lattice relaxation in twisted 2D materials and its effect on electronic structure.
motivation: To understand how lattice relaxation reshapes moiré flat bands and topological transitions in twisted systems.
method: Analytical modeling balancing intralayer elasticity and interlayer adhesion, embedded into moiré electronic Hamiltonians.
result: Reveals how relaxation shifts flat bands and topological transitions toward experimentally relevant twist angles.
conclusion: Provides a physically transparent framework for incorporating relaxation effects into moiré band structure calculations.

title: Bosonic Holes In Quadratic Bosonic Systems
authors: Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Hole degrees of freedom play a central role in the exact solution of quadratic (mean-field) systems. Although a variety of experiments have suggested the existence of bosonic holes, a consistent and complete theory has long been hindered by the ghost problems. Here, we resolve the ghost problem and …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224305] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves the ghost problem in quadratic bosonic systems and develops a consistent theory of bosonic holes.
motivation: Bosonic holes have been suggested by experiments but lacked a consistent theory due to ghost problems.
method: The authors resolve the ghost problem and provide a complete theoretical framework for bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.
result: A consistent and complete theory of bosonic holes is established, resolving the long-standing ghost problem.
conclusion: The work provides a solid theoretical foundation for understanding bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.

title: Topological Phase Transitions In Twisted Bilayer graphene/hBN From Interlayer Coupling And Substrate Potentials
authors: Huiwen Wang And Wei Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Huiwen Wang and Wei Jiang

Twisted bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride (TBG/hBN) hosts rich topological and correlated quantum phases, such as (fractional) Chern insulators, whose character is dictated by the topology of the moiré flat band. This topology is highly sensitive to several material parameters in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235109] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN, focusing on the effect of interlayer coupling and substrate potentials on moiré flat band topology.
motivation: Understanding how material parameters control the topology of moiré flat bands is crucial for engineering correlated and topological phases in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN systems.
method: The authors use a continuum model to compute the band structure and topological invariants (Chern numbers) as a function of interlayer coupling strength and substrate potential parameters.
result: They identify phase transitions between Chern insulator phases and trivial phases, mapping out phase diagrams that show how topology depends on the interplay of coupling and substrate.
conclusion: The topology of moiré flat bands in TBG/hBN can be tuned via interlayer coupling and substrate potentials, providing a route to control quantum phases in these systems.

title: Real-space Decay Of Flat-band Projectors From Compact Localized States
authors: Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, And Alexei Andreanov
abstract:
Author(s): Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, and Alexei Andreanov

Flat bands (FBs) with compact localized eigenstates (CLSs) fall into three main categories, controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set: orthogonal, linearly independent, and linearly dependent (singular). A CLS parametrization allows us to continuously tune a linearly independent FB into …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235110] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the real-space decay of flat-band projectors from compact localized states in flat-band systems.
motivation: Understanding the algebraic properties of compact localized states (CLS) and their projectors is important for characterizing flat-band systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors classify flat bands into three categories based on CLS properties and analyze the decay of projectors using a CLS parametrization.
result: They show that the decay of projectors is controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set, with singular CLS leading to slower decay.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of flat-band projectors but remains within condensed matter physics without clear relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Strange Metal Behavior In A Toy Model With Selective Mottness
authors: M. S. Laad And S. R. Hassan
abstract:
Author(s): M. S. Laad and S. R. Hassan

The interplay between band and atomic aspects in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states, or wide-band and effectively dispersionless electronic states is increasingly expected to lead to novel behavior. Using dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), we investigate strange metal-like beh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235111] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses DMFT to study strange metal behavior in a toy model with coexisting wide and flat bands, focusing on selective Mottness.
motivation: Strange metal behavior in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states is not well understood; the authors aim to model this using a toy model.
method: Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) is applied to a toy model with selective Mottness to investigate strange metal-like behavior.
result: The model reproduces strange metal characteristics such as linear-in-temperature resistivity and non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: Selective Mottness in a toy model can capture key features of strange metal behavior, providing insights into correlated electron systems.

title: Accurate Computation Of The Energy Variance For Ground States And $〈〈{\mathcal{L}}^{†}\mathcal{L}〉〉$ For Steady States Using iPEPS
authors: Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, And Philippe Corboz
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, and Philippe Corboz

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) provide a powerful tensor network ansatz for two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit. In this paper, we introduce an approach to accurately compute the energy variance of an iPEPS, enabling systematic extrapolations of the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245114] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to compute energy variance for ground states and steady states using infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) for 2D quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Accurate computation of energy variance is important for systematic extrapolations of ground state energies and for studying steady states of open quantum systems, but existing iPEPS methods lack precision.
method: The authors develop an approach to compute the energy variance of an iPEPS by contracting appropriate tensor networks, and also extend it to compute the expectation value of L†L for steady states of Lindblad master equations.
result: The method yields accurate energy variances for ground states and steady states, enabling reliable extrapolations and improved characterization of iPEPS approximations.
conclusion: The proposed technique enhances the utility of iPEPS for studying 2D quantum systems, particularly for assessing the quality of ground state approximations and for open system steady states.

title: Environment-matrix-product Operator For Boundary-free Large-scale Quantum Many-body Simulations
authors: Souta Shimozono And Chisa Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Souta Shimozono and Chisa Hotta

We propose an alternative to the infinite density-matrix renormalization approach for accessing quantum many-body states within a finite-size calculation that faithfully mimics the thermodynamic limit. Our method constructs environment-matrix-product operators (environment-MPOs) representing the Ham…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an environment-matrix-product operator method for boundary-free large-scale quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: To simulate quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit without finite-size effects, overcoming limitations of infinite DMRG.
method: Constructs environment-MPOs representing the Hamiltonian of a finite-size system that mimics the thermodynamic limit, using a boundary-free approach.
result: The method enables accurate simulation of large-scale quantum many-body systems with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The environment-MPO approach is a viable alternative to infinite DMRG for boundary-free simulations.

title: Update Of Hartree-Fock Theory For Hubbard-like Models
authors: E. Langmann And J. Lenells
abstract:
Author(s): E. Langmann and J. Lenells

We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitative errors in established condensed matter results.
motivation: Standard Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard models yields incorrect results; the authors aim to provide a corrected formulation.
method: The authors revisit and update the restricted Hartree-Fock formalism for Fermi Hubbard-like models, deriving corrected mean-field equations.
result: They show that previous textbook results are qualitatively wrong and present corrected solutions.
conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard treatment for Hubbard-like models in condensed matter physics.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond extended and localized states, specifically the emergence of multiple critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, using numerical methods to characterize phase transitions.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals new reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They show that the system can host topological phases and gauge-invariant dynamics, with potential for observing anyonic excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental platform for simulating topological gauge theories and studying their properties.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms
authors: Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, and Oded Zilberberg

The Kondo effect is a paradigmatic model of strongly correlated physics, where a magnetic impurity forms a many-body singlet with a fermionic environment. The properties of this singlet depend sensitively on correlations within the environment, which are particularly pronounced in one dimension, whe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023244] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo physics in one-dimensional quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with manifestations in ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, especially with a repulsive impurity.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo singlet formation and its properties in quantum wires.
result: They find that the repulsive impurity leads to distinct Kondo signatures that can be observed in ytterbium atom experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to realize and detect Kondo physics in quantum wires with repulsive impurities.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A new neural network architecture combining convolutional and transformer layers for representing quantum wave functions, achieving high accuracy on frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Improve variational wave function representations for quantum many-body systems, especially those with strong frustration or time-dependent behavior.
method: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function that respects lattice symmetries and uses attention mechanisms to capture long-range correlations.
result: Sets new accuracy benchmarks for ground states of frustrated magnets and for simulating quantum dynamics.
conclusion: The architecture is a powerful tool for quantum many-body problems, but the paper focuses on computational methods rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts

However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic techniques for gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS), focusing on gauge fixing and translation invariance in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative phenomena but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods offer an alternative, but handling gauge symmetry and translation invariance algorithmically is challenging.
method: The authors propose algorithms for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in Gaussian fermionic PEPS, leveraging the structure of Gaussian states to efficiently represent and manipulate gauge-invariant states.
result: They demonstrate that their gauge fixing and translation invariance algorithms work effectively for small systems, enabling the construction of translation-invariant gauge-invariant PEPS.
conclusion: The work provides algorithmic tools for simulating lattice gauge theories with tensor networks, but the focus is on computational methods rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy to quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework to simplify the problem.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and relates this to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of how space-time duality connects to exactly solvable dynamics and quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit models.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior, but the field is still developing; further research is needed for quantum applications.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.

method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including mean-field theory or exact diagonalization, to study the Kitaev model with Stone-Wales defects.
result: They find that a finite density of defects leads to a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids at finite temperature, providing a new route to realize these exotic phases in materials.

title: Persistence Of The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition With Long-Range Couplings
authors: Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, And Johannes Knolle
abstract:

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition is an archetypal example of a topological phase transition, which is driven by the proliferation of vortices. In this Letter, we analyze the persistence of the BKT transition in the XY model under the influence of long-range algebraically decaying…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227102] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the XY model with long-range couplings, focusing on the persistence of the topological phase transition.
motivation: The BKT transition is a key example of a topological phase transition, and understanding its behavior under long-range interactions is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze the XY model with algebraically decaying long-range couplings using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the BKT transition persists for a range of long-range coupling exponents, with modifications to the critical properties.
conclusion: Long-range couplings do not destroy the BKT transition but alter its characteristics, providing insight into topological phase transitions in non-local systems.

title: Crossed Surface Flat Bands In Three-Dimensional Superconducting Altermagnets
authors: Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, And Jorge Cayao

method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations for a three-dimensional altermagnetic superconductor.
result: Zero-energy surface crossed flat bands emerge due to the combined altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of topological surface states in altermagnetic superconductors, relevant for condensed matter physics.

title: Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Edelstein Effect
authors: Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, And Jian Wang

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect where both electric and magnetic fields generate spin magnetization, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To propose a new mechanism for generating spin magnetization beyond the conventional electric-field-only Edelstein effect.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model system to demonstrate the cooperative effect of electric and magnetic fields on spin magnetization.
result: The nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect is predicted, showing spin magnetization induced by combined fields.
conclusion: This work introduces a distinct mechanism for spin generation, relevant to spintronics but not to the user's research interests.

title: Acoustic Bound Pair States In The Continuum Induced By Off-Site Two-Body Interactions
authors: Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu

tldr: This paper reports the observation of acoustic bound states in the continuum induced by off-site two-body interactions in a classical phononic crystal simulating a quantum Bose-Hubbard model.
motivation: To demonstrate a novel many-body bound state in the continuum that arises solely from uniform off-site interactions, which has not been observed before.
method: The authors map a one-dimensional quantum Bose-Hubbard model with off-site interactions onto a two-dimensional macroscopic phononic crystal and experimentally observe the bound states.
result: They observe acoustic bound states in the continuum induced entirely by off-site two-body interactions, confirmed by both simulation and experiment.
conclusion: The work provides a classical analog of a quantum many-body phenomenon, offering a platform to study interaction-induced bound states in the continuum.

title: Edge Modes On Stringy Horizons
authors: Atish Dabholkar, Eleanor Harris, And Upamanyu Moitra
abstract:

For a quantum field of arbitrary mass and spin in the static patch of de Sitter spacetime, the Euclidean partition function receives contributions from edge modes localized on the horizon, expressible in terms of the Harish-Chandra character of the de Sitter group. Considering the flat limit and sum…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221501] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies edge modes on de Sitter horizons using group theory and Euclidean path integrals.
motivation: To understand quantum field theory in de Sitter spacetime and the role of edge modes in horizon thermodynamics.
method: Euclidean path integral approach with Harish-Chandra characters of the de Sitter group.
result: The partition function receives contributions from edge modes localized on the horizon, expressible in terms of group characters.
conclusion: Edge modes provide a universal contribution to the entropy of de Sitter horizons, with implications for quantum gravity.

title: Swimming Against A Superfluid Flow: Self-Propulsion Via Vortex-Antivortex Shedding In A Quantum Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:

A superfluid flows without friction below a critical velocity, exhibiting zero drag force on impurities. Above this threshold, superfluidity breaks down, and the internal energy is redistributed into incoherent excitations such as vortices. We demonstrate that a mobile, finite-mass impurity immersed…

tldr: A study of self-propulsion of a finite-mass impurity in a quantum fluid of light via vortex-antivortex shedding above the critical superfluid velocity.
motivation: To understand the breakdown of superfluidity and the dynamics of impurities in quantum fluids, with potential applications in quantum hydrodynamics.
method: Theoretical and numerical analysis of a mobile impurity in a polariton condensate, modeling vortex-antivortex pair creation and shedding.
result: The impurity can self-propel by shedding vortex-antivortex pairs, achieving a steady-state velocity above the critical speed.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for self-propulsion in quantum fluids, analogous to classical swimming but in a superfluid context.

title: Nonlinear Optomagnetic Signature Of $d$-Wave Altermagnets
authors: Lijun Yang And Long Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Lijun Yang and Long Liang

Altermagnetism, a recently discovered collinear magnetic order with net zero magnetization but exhibiting spin-splitting band structure, has attracted much research interest due to the rich fundamental physics and possible applications. In this Letter, we investigate the optomagnetic response of [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226702] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the nonlinear optomagnetic response of d-wave altermagnets, a recently discovered collinear magnetic order.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit spin-splitting band structure with net zero magnetization, offering rich physics and potential applications; understanding their optomagnetic response is of interest.
method: The authors theoretically study the nonlinear optomagnetic signature using a model for d-wave altermagnets.
result: They identify a characteristic nonlinear optomagnetic signal that distinguishes altermagnets from conventional antiferromagnets.
conclusion: The work provides a way to detect and characterize altermagnets via optical means, advancing the study of this new magnetic phase.

title: Interlayer Self-Doping Multiferroics
authors: Shulin Zhong, Dacheng Tian, Shengyuan A. Yang, Lan Chen, Su-Huai Wei, And Yunhao Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Shulin Zhong, Dacheng Tian, Shengyuan A. Yang, Lan Chen, Su-Huai Wei, and Yunhao Lu

Multiferroic materials, which simultaneously exhibit ferroelectric and magnetic orders, offer tremendous potential for next-generation electronic and spintronic devices. motivation: Multiferroics with coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders are promising for next-generation devices, but existing materials are limited.
method: First-principles calculations to design a heterostructure where charge transfer between layers induces both ferroelectricity and magnetism.
result: Demonstrates that interlayer self-doping can stabilize multiferroic order in a model system.
conclusion: This design principle may enable new multiferroic materials for spintronics and electronics.

title: Multipolar Orbital Relaxation Of The ${t}_{2g}$ States

abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226801] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the relaxation rate of orbital dipolar and quadrupolar moments in t2g states due to short-range impurities, without spin-orbit coupling.

method: A nonperturbative analytical approach is used to compute the relaxation rate of orbital moments in the presence of short-range impurities.

title: Electron Recoil Via Sample Momentum Transfer In Optical-Mode Excitation
authors: Akira Yasuhara, Yamato Kirii, And Takumi Sannomiya
abstract:

method: Momentum-resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) is used to detect the momentum imparted to planar samples upon excitation of optical modes.
result: First direct evidence that electrons transfer measurable momentum to planar samples during mode excitation.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into electron-sample momentum exchange, relevant for nanoscale imaging and spectroscopy.

title: Macroscopic Illusion And Microscopic Reality Of Glass Formation Paths: Cooling Vs Compression
authors: Kajetan Koperwas, Żaneta Wojnarowska, And Marian Paluch

We provide evidence that dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids may follow different microscopic routes under cooling and compression, pointing to a previously unrecognized discrepancy between two dynamical landmarks: the Arrhenius–to–non-Arrhenius crossover associated with cooling and the infl…

tldr: This paper studies the microscopic dynamics of glass formation under cooling versus compression, revealing a discrepancy in the Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius crossover.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental mechanisms of glass formation is important for materials science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids using experimental or simulation data, comparing cooling and compression pathways.
result: They find that the dynamical landmarks (e.g., Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius crossover) differ between cooling and compression, indicating different microscopic routes.
conclusion: The work highlights a previously unrecognized discrepancy in glass formation paths, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Entropic Charge Separation As A General Mechanism Arresting Nanoscale Condensate Coarsening
authors: Feipeng Chen, Jiaxing Yuan, Yaojun Zhang, Hajime Tanaka, And Ho Cheung Shum
abstract:

Size-dependent electrostatic barriers place an upper limit on droplet merging efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 228202] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electrostatic barriers that limit droplet merging in nanoscale condensates, using entropic charge separation as a mechanism.
motivation: Understanding and controlling coarsening in nanoscale condensates is important for applications in materials science and biology.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating size-dependent electrostatic barriers and validate it with experiments or simulations.
result: They find that entropic charge separation creates an upper limit on droplet merging efficiency, arresting coarsening.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a general principle for stabilizing nanoscale droplets against coalescence.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions

title: Altermagnetic And Dipolar Splitting Of Magnons In ${\mathrm{FeF}}_{2}$
