title: Ab Initio Superfluid Weight And Superconducting Penetration Depth
authors: Kaja H. Hiorth, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Théo Cavignac, Kristjan Haule, Miguel A. L. Marques, And Päivi Törmä
abstract:
Author(s): Kaja H. Hiorth, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Théo Cavignac, Kristjan Haule, Miguel A. L. Marques, and Päivi Törmä

Machine learning and high-throughput screening approaches to superconductor discovery require physically meaningful descriptors that capture essential physics while remaining computationally tractable. The superfluid weight is an ideal descriptor as it is a prerequisite for superconductivity, determ…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224509] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning and high-throughput screening to compute superfluid weight and penetration depth for superconductor discovery.
motivation: To accelerate superconductor discovery by identifying physically meaningful descriptors that are computationally tractable.
method: Combines ab initio calculations with machine learning models to predict superfluid weight and penetration depth from material properties.
result: Demonstrates that superfluid weight is a viable descriptor for high-throughput screening of superconductors.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively predict superconducting properties, aiding in the discovery of new superconductors.

title: Randomly Twisted Bilayer Graphene: Cascade Transitions
authors: Baruch Horovitz And Pierre Le Doussal
abstract:
Author(s): Baruch Horovitz and Pierre Le Doussal

Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is known to have disorder in its twist angle. We show that in terms of a Dirac equation with a random gauge potential [MATH], this disorder becomes huge when the average twist angle is near the magic angle where the Dirac velocity vanishes. The densit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies disorder effects in twisted bilayer graphene near the magic angle using a random gauge potential model.
motivation: Twisted bilayer graphene exhibits strong correlations at magic angles, but disorder in the twist angle can significantly affect its properties.
method: The authors model the system with a Dirac equation incorporating a random gauge potential and analyze the density of states and transport properties.
result: They find that disorder becomes huge near the magic angle, leading to cascade transitions in the density of states.
conclusion: Disorder in the twist angle is a crucial factor that must be considered in understanding the physics of twisted bilayer graphene.

title: Gaussian Expansion Method For Trions In Two-dimensional Materials
authors: Luiz G. M. Tenório, André J. Chaves, Emiko Hiyama, And Tobias Frederico
abstract:
Author(s): Luiz G. M. Tenório, André J. Chaves, Emiko Hiyama, and Tobias Frederico

We investigate the properties of trions in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) monolayers using the Gaussian expansion method (GEM) adapted to two-dimensional systems. Excitons and trions in monolayer TMDCs with the chemical composition [MATH] in the 2H phase are studied systematically. We …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235411] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trions in TMDC monolayers using the Gaussian expansion method, focusing on their binding energies and properties.
motivation: Understanding trion properties in two-dimensional materials is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors adapt the Gaussian expansion method to two-dimensional systems and solve the Schrödinger equation for trions in TMDCs.
result: They compute binding energies and wavefunctions for excitons and trions, showing good agreement with experimental data.
conclusion: The Gaussian expansion method is effective for studying trions in 2D materials, but the work is purely computational condensed matter physics.

title: Conductance Anomaly In A Partially Open Adiabatic Quantum Point Contact
authors: Donghao Liu And Dmitri Gutman
abstract:
Author(s): Donghao Liu and Dmitri Gutman

We demonstrate that conductance anomalies can arise in a clean, adiabatic quantum point contact when a channel is partially transmitting. Even for a smooth barrier potential, backscattering induces Friedel oscillations that, via electron interactions, generate a singular correction to the conductanc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235412] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies conductance anomalies in a quantum point contact due to Friedel oscillations and electron interactions, a topic in mesoscopic physics.
motivation: Understanding conductance anomalies in clean quantum point contacts is important for interpreting transport experiments, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter phenomenon without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze backscattering and Friedel oscillations in an adiabatic quantum point contact, incorporating electron interactions to compute singular corrections to conductance.
result: They find that even for a smooth barrier, backscattering leads to Friedel oscillations that, via interactions, produce a singular correction to the conductance, explaining observed anomalies.
conclusion: Conductance anomalies can arise from intrinsic interaction effects in clean point contacts, without requiring disorder or other extrinsic mechanisms.

title: Anomalies In The Thermal Conductivity Of The Honeycomb Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS}}_{3}$
authors: Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, And Minoru Yamashita
abstract:
Author(s): Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-ichi Yamaura, and Minoru Yamashita

Intrinsic two-dimensional magnets serve as a good platform to explore collective, charge-neutral, and low-energy excitations. Distinguishing their crucial role in the experimental aspect remains a challenge for decades. Here, we study the thermal transport in honeycomb antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport anomalies in the honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS3, focusing on low-energy excitations.
motivation: To understand the role of collective charge-neutral excitations in thermal transport of two-dimensional magnets.
method: Thermal conductivity measurements on MnPS3 single crystals as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: Observed anomalies in thermal conductivity attributed to magnon and possibly spinon contributions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of magnetic excitations in thermal transport of 2D antiferromagnets.

title: Mass-induced Coulomb Drag In Capacitively Coupled Superconducting Nanowires
authors: Aleksandr Latyshev, Adrien Tomà, And Eugene V. Sukhorukov
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksandr Latyshev, Adrien Tomà, and Eugene V. Sukhorukov

We investigate Coulomb drag in a system of two capacitively coupled superconducting nanowires. In this context, drag refers to the appearance of a stationary voltage in the passive wire in response to a current bias applied to the active one. Quantum phase slips in the biased wire generate voltage f…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245410] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Coulomb drag in capacitively coupled superconducting nanowires driven by quantum phase slips.
motivation: To understand drag effects in superconducting nanowires and the role of quantum phase slips in generating voltage in a passive wire.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of two capacitively coupled nanowires, treating quantum phase slips as the source of voltage fluctuations that induce drag.
result: Coulomb drag arises from mass (phase-slip) fluctuations, leading to a drag voltage proportional to the bias current and coupling strength.
conclusion: Quantum phase slips in superconducting nanowires can mediate Coulomb drag, providing a new mechanism for drag in low-dimensional superconductors.

title: Theory Of Sondheimer Magneto-oscillations Beyond The Semiclassical Limit
authors: Alexander Nikolaenko And Pavel A. Nosov
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Nikolaenko and Pavel A. Nosov

In conducting films subjected to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion along the field direction gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in field intensity—a phenomenon known as Sondheimer oscillations. Traditionally, these oscillations were understood within the semiclassical fram…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245411] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the theory of Sondheimer magneto-oscillations in conducting films beyond the semiclassical limit.
motivation: Sondheimer oscillations are a quantum phenomenon in thin films under magnetic fields, but previous semiclassical treatments fail in certain regimes; a full quantum theory is needed.
method: The authors develop a quantum mechanical theory for electron motion in a thin film with an out-of-plane magnetic field, going beyond the semiclassical approximation.
result: They derive new expressions for conductance oscillations that capture quantum corrections and predict deviations from the semiclassical result.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate theoretical framework for understanding Sondheimer oscillations, relevant for interpreting experiments in mesoscopic systems.

title: Phase-sensitive Nonreciprocal Transport In High-temperature Superconductors
authors: Guo-Liang Guo And Xin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Guo-Liang Guo and Xin Liu

We propose the superconducting diode effect (SDE) in a planar [MATH]-wave/[MATH]-wave/[MATH]-wave Josephson junction as a direct phase-sensitive probe of the [MATH]-wave pairing function in high-[MATH] superconductors. Asymmetric interface coupling breaks inversion symmetry and induces a spontaneous [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220501] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting diode effect in a d-wave/d-wave/d-wave Josephson junction as a phase-sensitive probe of d-wave pairing in high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: To directly probe the d-wave pairing symmetry in high-temperature superconductors using a phase-sensitive transport phenomenon.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a planar d-wave/d-wave/d-wave Josephson junction with asymmetric interface coupling, which breaks inversion symmetry and induces a spontaneous phase shift, leading to nonreciprocal critical currents.
result: They demonstrate that the superconducting diode effect can serve as a direct phase-sensitive probe of the d-wave pairing function, with the diode efficiency depending on the junction geometry and interface asymmetry.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a new method to identify d-wave pairing in high-Tc superconductors via nonreciprocal transport.

title: Interaction-induced Quasicrystalline Order: Emergence Of Quasisolid And Quasisupersolid Phases
authors: Chao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Zhang

Deterministic quasiperiodicity in quantum systems has long been associated with localization, criticality, or glassy behavior, and has therefore been believed to suppress long-range order rather than stabilize it. Here, we demonstrate the opposite: quasiperiodicity in interactions—without any quasip…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220502] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quasiperiodicity in interactions can stabilize quasicrystalline order, leading to quasisolid and quasisupersolid phases.
motivation: Deterministic quasiperiodicity was believed to suppress long-range order; this work challenges that by demonstrating the opposite effect in interacting systems.
method: The authors study a model with quasiperiodic interactions and analyze the emergence of quasicrystalline order using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that interaction-induced quasiperiodicity can stabilize quasisolid and quasisupersolid phases, which exhibit both crystalline and superfluid properties.
conclusion: Quasiperiodicity in interactions can be a mechanism to create novel ordered phases, expanding the understanding of quasicrystals in quantum systems.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric linearization principle, providing a dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions appear in many complex systems, but a consistent dynamical foundation is lacking.
method: The authors introduce a linearization principle at the dynamical level, using geometric arguments to derive the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation.
result: A geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations is presented, linking the linearization principle to observed anomalous diffusion.
conclusion: The work offers a new geometric perspective on nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, potentially unifying descriptions of complex systems.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where standard diffusion models fail, especially under external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift, deriving mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
result: The model captures subdiffusive, superdiffusive, and normal diffusion regimes depending on the waiting-time distribution parameters and bias strength.
conclusion: Biased CTRWs with asymmetric waiting times provide a versatile framework for anomalous diffusion in the presence of drift, relevant to biological and soft matter systems.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics arguments to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds that the critical temperature is bounded above by a universal number determined by the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Minority Takeover In Majority Dynamics: Searching For Rare Initializations Via The History Passing Algorithm
authors: Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, And Lenka Zdeborová
abstract:
Author(s): Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, and Lenka Zdeborová

We investigate how much bias in the initial configuration is required to drive global agreement in synchronous, deterministic majority dynamics on large random [MATH]-regular graphs. Nodes take values [MATH] and update their states at each discrete time step to align with the majority of their neighbors.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how initial bias affects global agreement in majority dynamics on random regular graphs, using a history passing algorithm.
motivation: Understanding the minimal bias needed for a minority to take over in majority dynamics is relevant to social networks and distributed computing.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on large random d-regular graphs and propose a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations.
result: They find that a small initial bias can lead to global agreement, and the history passing algorithm efficiently identifies such configurations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the sensitivity of majority dynamics to initial conditions and offers a computational tool for studying rare events.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws.
motivation: To understand learning dynamics and catastrophic forgetting in physical neural networks implemented as resistor networks.
method: The authors use differentiable resistor networks where learning occurs via interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints.
result: They investigate sequential learning and observe catastrophic forgetting in these networks.
conclusion: The work provides insights into learning in physical systems but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic properties of a quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using a variational approach.
motivation: To understand the phase diagram and critical behavior of a higher-spin quantum spin model with transverse crystal field, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A variational method based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state are employed.
result: Thermodynamic properties and phase boundaries are obtained for the spin-2 model.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the quantum Blume-Capel model but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically solves the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions, deriving the partition function and spontaneous magnetization.
motivation: To extend the exact solution of the 2D Ising model beyond nearest-neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Uses transfer matrices in Clifford algebraic, transfer matrix, and other representations to compute the partition function and magnetization analytically.
result: Obtains closed-form expressions for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization for the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
conclusion: The work provides an exact solution for a more complex Ising model, contributing to the theory of phase transitions and statistical mechanics.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, focusing on biologically relevant finite-size effects.
motivation: The model extends the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) to include pausing particles, originally motivated by RNA polymerase dynamics during transcription.
method: The authors extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate equivalence to a model with dynamical defects, analyzing finite-size effects.
result: They provide a comprehensive study of the pTASEP, showing how pausing and defects affect particle transport and density profiles.
conclusion: The work offers insights into biological transport processes but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Granger Causality Maps For Langevin Systems
authors: Lionel Barnett, Benjamin Wahl, Nadine Spychala, And Anil K. Seth
abstract:
Author(s): Lionel Barnett, Benjamin Wahl, Nadine Spychala, and Anil K. Seth

Wahl et al. [
tldr: This paper introduces Granger causality maps for Langevin systems, a method to infer causal relationships in stochastic dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal structure in complex dynamical systems is important for many fields, but the paper focuses on a classical stochastic framework.
method: The authors extend the concept of Granger causality to Langevin systems by locally linearizing dynamics as vector Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and computing GCs on phase space.
result: They demonstrate that GC maps can be constructed for Langevin systems, providing a way to visualize causal influences in phase space.
conclusion: The work contributes to causal inference in stochastic systems but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relaxation Of The Random Site Coulomb Glass Model In Two Dimensions
authors: Preeti Bhandari And Vikas Malik
abstract:
Author(s): Preeti Bhandari and Vikas Malik

This study investigates the influence of material density, disorder in onsite energies, and localization length on relaxation dynamics within a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling. To explore relaxation laws, we calculate the eigenvalue distribution of the linear dynamica…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064107] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies relaxation dynamics in a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model, focusing on the effects of disorder and localization length on eigenvalue distributions.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in disordered systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically compute eigenvalue distributions of the linear dynamical matrix for the Coulomb glass model at half-filling, varying density, disorder, and localization length.
result: They find that relaxation laws depend on the parameters, with eigenvalue distributions showing characteristic features of the Coulomb glass.
conclusion: The study provides insights into relaxation in disordered electronic systems but remains within classical condensed matter physics without quantum or thermodynamic implications.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms behind blue-detuned MOTs for molecules is important for advancing molecular cooling and trapping techniques.
method: The authors analyze a blue-detuned MOT driven by two closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization, using theoretical modeling to identify the role of dark states and Zeeman splitting.
result: They find that when Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference, a state is dark to one beam but not the other, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.
conclusion: The identified mechanisms explain how trapping and cooling occur in blue-detuned molecular MOTs, which could improve molecular cooling methods.

title: Quantum-enhanced T-stochastic Neighbor Embedding For High-dimensional Data Visualization
authors: Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, And Song Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, and Song Lin

t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that preserves local similarity by matching probability distributions between high- and low-dimensional spaces. Owing to its ability to capture complex manifold structures, t-SNE has become a widely…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023265] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced version of t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization using quantum amplitude estimation and Grover's search.
motivation: Classical t-SNE is computationally expensive for large datasets; quantum algorithms may offer speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that replaces classical gradient computation with quantum amplitude estimation and uses Grover's search for nearest neighbor finding.
result: The quantum t-SNE achieves quadratic speedup in the number of data points and dimensions compared to classical t-SNE.
conclusion: Quantum computing can accelerate nonlinear dimensionality reduction, but practical implementation requires fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, and Nicolás Morales-Durán

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials is crucial for realizing topological phases, but Berry curvature inhomogeneity can disrupt them.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation to study the effect of Berry curvature on many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the many-body gap and can drive a transition from fractional Chern insulator to charge density wave.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor destabilizing fractional Chern insulators, explaining experimental observations in moiré materials.

title: Reducibility Of Higher-order To Pairwise Interactions: Social Impact Models On Hypergraphs
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, And Federico Vázquez
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, and Federico Vázquez

We show that a general class of node-update social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly mapped to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network. This mapping preserves the microscopic probabilities of changing the state of the no…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023250] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that a class of social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly reduced to pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network.
motivation: Higher-order interactions are common in social systems but are computationally complex; the authors aim to simplify such models without losing microscopic accuracy.
method: They prove an exact mapping from a general class of node-update social impact models on hypergraphs to equivalent models with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network.
result: The mapping preserves the microscopic probabilities of state changes, enabling the use of standard pairwise network analysis tools.
conclusion: Higher-order social impact models can be effectively reduced to pairwise models, simplifying analysis while maintaining fidelity.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: To efficiently simulate dense active matter systems where traditional methods are slow due to small time steps.
method: Extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian particles, using a cluster algorithm that handles steric interactions via event chains.
result: The algorithm shows improved computational efficiency compared to standard Brownian dynamics for active matter systems.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm is a promising tool for simulating active matter with steric interactions, enabling larger-scale studies.

title: Reproducible Nucleation And Control Of Stable Quantum Vortex Rings In Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, And Luca Galantucci
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, and Luca Galantucci

Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid systems under clean and controlled conditions emerges as a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research. This work introduces an experimentally feasible protocol for the on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings in harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates, systematically investigating how the protocol setup influences the ring dynamics and proposing a method to generate vortex excitations such as Kelvin waves.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022043] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for nucleating and controlling stable quantum vortex rings in Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluids is a key challenge in quantum fluid research.
method: The authors propose an experimentally feasible protocol using harmonically trapped cylindrical BECs and systematically investigate how the setup influences ring dynamics.
result: They demonstrate on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings and a method to generate Kelvin waves.
conclusion: The protocol enables controlled studies of vortex dynamics in clean superfluid systems.

title: Compression, Simulation, And Synthesis Of Turbulent Flows With Tensor Trains
authors: Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, and Leandro Aolita

Numerical simulations of turbulent fluids are paramount to real-life applications, from predicting and modeling flows to diagnostic purposes in engineering. However, they are also computationally challenging due to their intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, which require a very high spatial resolution …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023245] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies tensor train decompositions to compress, simulate, and synthesize turbulent fluid flows, demonstrating computational speedups.
motivation: Turbulent flow simulations are computationally expensive due to high spatial resolution requirements; tensor methods offer a way to reduce complexity.
method: The authors use tensor train (TT) decompositions to represent turbulent flow data and perform numerical simulations within the TT format, leveraging low-rank structure.
result: They achieve significant compression ratios and speedups in simulation time while maintaining accuracy for certain turbulent flow regimes.
conclusion: Tensor train methods are a promising tool for reducing computational costs in turbulence modeling, though applicability depends on flow characteristics.

title: Straintronics And Twistronics In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, And Zhen Zhan
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, and Zhen Zhan

The interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene enables the formation of moiré patterns and narrow bands that host correlated and topological phases. While magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has been widely studied, strain provides an additional and realistic control knob for band engineerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023225] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene to engineer moiré patterns and narrow bands for correlated and topological phases.
motivation: To explore strain as an additional control knob beyond twist angle for band engineering in bilayer graphene, enabling new correlated and topological phases.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of strained and twisted bilayer graphene, analyzing band structures and moiré patterns.
result: Strain can significantly modify the moiré pattern and narrow band properties, offering a tunable platform for correlated and topological phases.
conclusion: Straintronics and twistronics together provide a versatile approach to engineer quantum phases in bilayer graphene.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, with implications for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, likely using techniques from computational complexity theory and statistical physics.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial for predicting system behavior, but existing methods often lack a physical basis.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework accurately predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed causal inference can improve link prediction in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers at topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems beyond conventional integer and fractional quantum Hall effects.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches to study exciton condensation in bilayer quantum Hall systems.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluids with non-Abelian statistics and robust superfluidity.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for engineering anyonic superfluids, which may have implications for topological quantum computation.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transitions in frustrated magnetic systems, specifically kagome spin ice HoAgGe.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic order and critical behavior.
result: Observation of a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the exotic magnetic phases of kagome spin ice materials.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: The authors perform magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, on twisted bilayer WSe2 devices under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: They observe a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstrate electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall states and provides a method to control magnetic order electrically.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, and to explore their unique properties at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical exponents and correlation functions of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-gas critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusually calm behavior (suppressed fluctuations) yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The study reveals novel critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, which may have implications for materials with controlled density fluctuations.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: Experiments on disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale silicon photonic crystals were fabricated and their wave dynamics were studied experimentally, likely with optical measurements.
result: Unexpected residual scattering was observed, driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expected transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and point to radiative loss as a key factor.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a purely condensed matter physics result with no quantum information or thermodynamics angle.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable spin transport.
method: Encapsulated graphene devices are used to perform transverse magnetic focusing, measuring spin-dependent transport.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect, with gate-tunable spin coherence.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-based electron optics, but the work is focused on transport physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or experimental characterization to investigate the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic state and describe its properties.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of relaxor ferroelectrics but does not relate to the user's research interests.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of long-lived hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems and their unique excitations.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation combined with resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe polaronic and phononic excitations in Pr0.67Ca0.33MnO3.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with distinct polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium is generated.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable hidden phases with novel excitations in manganites, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium states in correlated materials.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: Increasing activity can counterintuitively reduce the solid's active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The percolation threshold governs the macroscopic active response, leading to a 'more is less' effect.

title: Physics-Based Factorized Machine Learning For Predicting Ionic Dielectric Tensors
authors: Atsushi Takigawa, Shin Kiyohara, And Yu Kumagai
abstract:
Author(s): Atsushi Takigawa, Shin Kiyohara, and Yu Kumagai

A machine-learning methodology helps screen thousands of candidate oxides to identify materials with excellent dielectric properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021006] Published Tue Apr 07, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning method predicts ionic dielectric tensors of oxides using physics-based factorization.
motivation: To accelerate the discovery of materials with high dielectric constants for electronic applications.
method: A factorized machine learning model that incorporates physical constraints to predict dielectric tensors from crystal structure.
result: The model accurately predicts dielectric tensors for thousands of oxides, identifying promising candidates.
conclusion: Physics-based machine learning can efficiently screen materials for dielectric properties, aiding materials discovery.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of elementary operations, including photon catalysis, which can be implemented with realistic experimental tools.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps, providing a universal and efficient state preparation scheme.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and systematic approach to photonic state preparation, potentially advancing photonic quantum computing and quantum networks.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: Covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and light-matter interactions.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving with new theoretical understanding, materials, and applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome lattice materials, analyzing electronic structure, many-body effects, and observed phenomena.
result: Identifies key mechanisms like sublattice interference, spin-orbit coupling, and frustration that lead to exotic states.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for studying correlated and topological physics, but the paper is primarily a materials-focused review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is important for many areas of physics.
method: The paper reviews experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale numerical simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: It highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation, and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with open questions, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological features.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising candidates, but further work is needed to confirm their existence and properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent work using maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural data, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further improvements in experimental sensitivity are needed.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A review of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in exotic geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling simulation of topological phenomena and gravitational models.
method: The paper surveys experimental and theoretical approaches for implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: It summarizes progress in realizing nonstandard geometries and discusses emergent phenomena like topological states and analogies to gravity.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential for simulating fundamental physics, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on how units align their orientation with their own velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active matter, which has implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables a spectrum of behaviors from single-particle orbiting to synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that can be harnessed for designing new materials and robotic systems.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity effects has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity and introduces Lorentz violation via work-producing legs, leading to late-time cosmological consequences.
motivation: To explore controlled violations of Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation within an emergent gravity framework, and to study their cosmological implications.
method: The authors model general relativity as a thermodynamic Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs, then add work-producing legs to generate Lorentz violation, analyzing the resulting cosmological dynamics.
result: The work-producing legs produce late-time cosmic acceleration and other observable signatures, providing a thermodynamic origin for dark energy.
conclusion: Lorentz violation in emergent gravity can explain dark energy and offers testable predictions for cosmology.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability

method: The authors fabricate nanoscale tips that generate coherent phonons with tunable frequencies and use them to probe functional materials.
result: They achieve broadband frequency tunability of coherent phonons at the nanoscale.
conclusion: The tunable coherent phonon tips provide a new approach for nanoscale characterization of material properties.

method: The authors use magnetically induced spin depolarization measurements in the n2EDM apparatus to infer the neutron energy spectrum and material-dependent storage properties.
result: The method successfully extracts the energy spectrum and provides sensitivity to storage properties of trap materials.

authors: Sichao Qu, Zixiong Yu, Erqian Dong, Min Yang, And Nicholas X. Fang

Sound wave scattering can be increased in one frequency range only by reducing scattering in another range, according to experiments—a discovery relevant for acoustic engineering.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an acoustic analogy of the quantum Baldin sum rule, demonstrating a trade-off in sound wave scattering across frequencies.
motivation: To explore fundamental limits in acoustic scattering, analogous to quantum sum rules, for optimal design of acoustic devices.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical modeling of sound wave scattering in engineered structures.
result: Scattering enhancement in one frequency range necessarily reduces scattering in another, confirming the sum rule.
conclusion: The acoustic Baldin sum rule provides a universal constraint for acoustic scattering, with implications for acoustic engineering.

tldr: This paper studies the boundary critical behavior of the 3D O(N) model using conformal bootstrap methods.
motivation: Understanding boundary universality classes in 3D O(N) models, particularly the extraordinary-log phase, is important for condensed matter physics.

conclusion: The results confirm and refine the understanding of boundary criticality in 3D O(N) models, but the work is purely in statistical/condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterization Of Feshbach Resonances In A $^{6}\mathrm{Li}−^{7}\mathrm{Li}$ Mixture Using Improved Interaction Potentials
authors: Jing-Chen Zhang (张京晨), Paul Julienne, And Yu Liu

We characterize Feshbach resonances in all isotopologs of the [MATH] system with improved interaction potentials. Starting from spectroscopically accurate Morse/long-range (MLR) potential-energy curves for the singlet [MATH] and triplet [MATH] ele…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062802] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Characterization of Feshbach resonances in a lithium isotope mixture using improved interaction potentials.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of Feshbach resonances is essential for controlling ultracold atomic interactions, but existing potentials for Li mixtures are insufficiently precise.
method: Constructed spectroscopically accurate Morse/long-range (MLR) potential-energy curves for singlet and triplet states, then calculated resonance positions and widths.
result: Predicted new Feshbach resonances and improved agreement with experimental data for 6Li-7Li mixtures.
conclusion: The improved potentials enable more precise control of atomic interactions, benefiting experiments in ultracold physics.

authors: Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, And Bin Qiao

tldr: Investigates coherent radiation from multielectron wave packets in intense laser fields using strong-field QED and density matrix formalism.
motivation: To understand and characterize coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams as a potential light source.
method: Uses density matrix formalism within strong-field QED to model a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse.
result: Derives general expressions for coherent radiation and analyzes the effects of electron correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for coherent radiation from multielectron systems, relevant for light source development.

method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), density functional theory (DFT), and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) were used to probe the electronic and magnetic properties.
result: Hybridized kagome bands and induced Ti magnetism were observed in R-Ti3-Bi4 compounds (R=Nd, Sm, Gd).
conclusion: The study provides detailed characterization of these kagome metals but does not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220103] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies ferroelectric domain wall dynamics driven by polarization currents and introduces ferrons as quanta of collective polarization excitations.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of ferroelectric textures under polarization currents and compare with magnon-driven domain wall motion.
method: Theoretical analysis mapping linear polarization excitations to ferrons and deriving the resulting force on domain walls.
result: Ferrons provide an exotic driving mechanism for domain wall dynamics distinct from magnonic counterparts.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of ferroelectric domain wall dynamics but is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

The van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnets with a large uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy (UMA) have compelling advantages for terahertz spintronics applications. Although the temperature dependence of UMA is essential for ensuring device endurance, it has scarcely been explored. Here, we unveil …

motivation: Understanding the temperature dependence of UMA is crucial for device endurance in terahertz spintronics applications, but it has been scarcely explored.
method: The authors perform experimental measurements and theoretical calculations to unveil the unconventional temperature dependence of UMA in FePS3.
result: They find an unconventional temperature dependence of UMA, which deviates from standard behavior.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the magnetic properties of FePS3, aiding its application in spintronics.

tldr: This paper reports the crystal growth and magnetic properties of a rare-earth triangular-lattice compound ErZn3P3, revealing fragile long-range antiferromagnetic order.
motivation: Rare-earth triangular lattices are platforms for novel quantum magnetic states, but the magnetic properties of ErZn3P3 were previously unexplored.
method: Single crystals were grown, and magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and neutron diffraction measurements were performed to characterize the magnetic order.
result: The compound exhibits long-range antiferromagnetic order below 2.2 K, but the order is fragile and easily suppressed by magnetic fields.
conclusion: ErZn3P3 is a candidate for studying frustrated magnetism and field-induced quantum phases in triangular lattices.

method: Transmission electron microscopy and transport measurements on 1T-TiSe2 nanoflakes of varying thicknesses to observe the charge density wave transition temperature.
result: The charge density wave melting temperature decreases with decreasing flake thickness, demonstrating size-dependent suppression of the ordered phase.
conclusion: Size effects play a significant role in electronic phase transitions, analogous to classical melting point depression, and must be considered in nanoscale correlated systems.

title: Micrometer-range Spin-wave Transport By Incorporating Perpendicular Spins In Artificial Spin Ice

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature.
