motivation: Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between different temperature replicas to improve sampling efficiency in continuous-space PIMC.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measured observables in benchmark simulations.
conclusion: The proposed EMC technique is effective for accelerating PIMC simulations of bosonic systems at finite temperature.

method: A network model where nodes represent communities with internal dynamics, coupled via migration-like interactions, analyzed using linear stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: The model exhibits diffusion-driven pattern formation analogous to Turing patterns, leading to stable spatial heterogeneity in opinions.
conclusion: Spatial coupling and network topology can sustain opinion diversity, with implications for social dynamics and complex systems.

tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in heterogeneous environments.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in heterogeneous media is important for transport in disordered systems and biological processes.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to derive FPT distributions for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
result: The FPT properties depend on the statistics of the diffusion coefficient, with explicit expressions for certain cases.

motivation: Understanding flow-driven self-organization in reaction-diffusion-advection systems is important for biological and chemical pattern formation.

authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff

result: Resetting can induce instability in the queue even when the underlying search process is stable, depending on resetting rate and queue parameters.

conclusion: Machine-learned potentials can be used to design and predict self-assembly of topological solitons, opening avenues for materials with knotted field configurations.

conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for exploring flat-band physics and strongly correlated phenomena without the need for cryogenic conditions.

method: The paper reviews various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to better predict and optimize photophysical properties in materials for photonics and energy harvesting.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022038] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies large deviations in non-Markovian stochastic epidemic models, focusing on outbreak-size distributions and disease lifetimes.
motivation: Understanding how non-exponential waiting-time distributions affect epidemic outcomes is important for public health modeling.
method: The authors analyze non-Markovian epidemic models in a well-mixed setting using large deviation theory.
result: They find that non-exponential waiting times significantly alter the final outbreak-size distribution and disease lifetime compared to Markovian models.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects are crucial for accurate epidemic modeling and should be incorporated into future studies.

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training processes.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: The authors use a vapor training process to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The vapor training process leads to improved plasticity and better shaping of the films.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work enhances the link between microscopic ion motion and macroscopic properties.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses and their relation to glass stability using inelastic x-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding the vibrational properties of glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal behavior, but the connection between glass stability and low-frequency vibrations is not well understood.
method: The authors use an improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure the vibrational density of states in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: They find that more stable glasses exhibit a suppression of low-frequency vibrational modes, indicating a link between glass stability and the boson peak.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the microscopic origin of the boson peak and the relationship between glass stability and vibrational dynamics.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the hydrodynamics of microbial motility is important for biology and microfluidics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors used experimental three-dimensional flow measurements to study the flow field around a free-swimming microalga.
result: They discovered unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena that expand understanding of microhydrodynamics.
conclusion: The findings have profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology, but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond driven by subsurface compliant regions.
motivation: Understanding and engineering mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond is important for applications, but this work is purely materials science.
method: Experimental characterization and modeling of nanodiamond mechanical response under strain.
result: Subsurface compliant regions enable elastic deformation in nanodiamond, with size-dependent effects.
conclusion: The findings provide a method to engineer mechanical properties of diamond, but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, and Huaizhou Zhao

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free method to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials can convert waste heat to electricity, but traditional doping methods have limitations. A doping-free approach is sought to boost performance.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, and characterize the resulting thermoelectric properties.
result: The self-doping significantly improves the thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) compared to conventionally doped samples.
conclusion: Phase-transition-induced self-doping is an effective strategy for enhancing thermoelectric performance without external dopants.

title: Nearly Isotropic Upper Critical Field In Pressurized Trilayer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10−δ}$
authors: Di Peng et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Di Peng et al.

Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure reveal an isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelates driven by the compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021008] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: Angle-dependent magnetotransport under pressure reveals isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelate superconductor.
motivation: To understand the superconducting pairing mechanism in nickelates by measuring the upper critical field anisotropy.
method: High-pressure magnetotransport measurements with angle dependence on La4Ni3O10−δ single crystals.
result: The upper critical field is nearly isotropic, suggesting a dominant role of interlayer coupling or orbital compensation.
conclusion: The isotropic behavior indicates a three-dimensional superconducting state, possibly driven by both in-plane and out-of-plane orbitals.

title: Targeted Calibration To Adjust Stability Biases In Complex Dynamical System Models
authors: Daniel Pals, Sebastian Bathiany, Joel Kuettel, Richard A. Wood, And Niklas Boers
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Pals, Sebastian Bathiany, Joel Kuettel, Richard A. Wood, and Niklas Boers

A method is introduced for systematic calibration of complex dynamical system models, targeted at adjusting system stability, with applications to climate models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021007] Published Tue Apr 07, 2026.
tldr: A method for calibrating complex dynamical system models to adjust stability biases, applied to climate models.
motivation: Complex dynamical system models often have stability biases that affect predictions; systematic calibration is needed.
method: The authors introduce a targeted calibration technique that adjusts model parameters to correct stability biases.
result: The method is demonstrated on climate models, showing improved stability and prediction accuracy.
conclusion: Targeted calibration can effectively reduce stability biases in complex dynamical system models.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper reviews both experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It summarizes the current understanding of how pressure affects the electronic structure and properties of these materials.
conclusion: The review highlights the challenges and advances in studying these radioactive, complex materials, expanding knowledge of their behavior.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the interdisciplinary nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No new scientific results; a retrospective on the development of neural networks and physics.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can inspire discoveries across disciplines.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel Lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning, not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines, which are stochastic neural networks that learn probability distributions.
method: Hinton describes the architecture of Boltzmann machines, the contrastive divergence learning algorithm, and their connection to statistical physics.
result: Boltzmann machines were influential in the early days of deep learning, enabling unsupervised learning of latent representations.
conclusion: The lecture highlights the interdisciplinary impact of Boltzmann machines, bridging physics and machine learning, but does not address quantum or thermodynamic information processing.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The review highlights capabilities and limitations of each technique and cases where they complement each other.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a more comprehensive understanding of atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Nuclear reactions in stars are crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many have very small rates at low energies, making direct measurement difficult.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques to study them on Earth.
result: Summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory and proposes new ideas for laboratory measurements.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical phenomena dominate stellar nuclear reactions, and further theoretical and experimental work is needed to understand them.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improved uncertainties.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global set of data from physics and chemistry experiments, taking into account correlations and uncertainties up to the end of 2022.
result: A self-consistent set of values and conversion factors for fundamental constants is provided, with updated uncertainties.
conclusion: The CODATA 2022 values serve as the internationally recommended reference for fundamental constants.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep into tissues.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed to provide biological and clinical insight into cells and tissues at depth with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, where short laser pulses are absorbed by tissue, causing a temperature rise that generates ultrasound waves detected by external sensors.
result: Optoacoustic imaging can achieve high-resolution imaging at depths of millimeters to centimeters, and recent developments combine it with optical techniques for multimodal microscopy.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a powerful noninvasive imaging tool with significant potential for biological and clinical research.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling accurate and insightful materials simulations.

title: Observable Gravitational Wave Strain At Second Order
authors: Guillem Domènech, Shi Pi (皮石), And Ao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Domènech, Shi Pi (皮石), and Ao Wang (王奥)

The ambiguity in associating gravitational waves with transverse-traceless components of the metric at second order in perturbation theory is resolved by computing the detector response to second order for the first time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves the ambiguity in associating gravitational waves with transverse-traceless metric components at second order in perturbation theory by computing the detector response to second order.
motivation: The ambiguity in defining gravitational waves at second order in perturbation theory needed resolution to correctly interpret observable signals.
method: The authors compute the detector response to second order in perturbation theory for the first time.
result: They show that the observable strain measured by a detector corresponds to the transverse-traceless part of the metric at second order, resolving the ambiguity.
conclusion: The work clarifies the definition of observable gravitational wave strain at second order, which is important for accurate detection and interpretation.

title: One-Jettiness Distribution Contains Super-Super-Leading Logarithms
authors: Andrea Banfi, Jeffrey R. Forshaw, And Jack Holguin
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Banfi, Jeffrey R. Forshaw, and Jack Holguin

We show that one-jettiness ([MATH]) in color-singlet plus jet production suffers from superleading logarithms starting at order [MATH] relative to the Born level. This is one logarithm more dominant than any previously identified superleading logarithms…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221901] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies super-super-leading logarithms in one-jettiness for color-singlet plus jet production in high-energy QCD.
motivation: To understand the structure of logarithmic enhancements in jet observables beyond known super-leading logarithms.
method: Analytical resummation and fixed-order calculations in perturbative QCD.
result: Discovery of super-super-leading logarithms at order α_s^4 relative to Born, which are more dominant than previously known super-leading logarithms.

title: Unveiling Spin And Poynting Dual Textures Of An Optical Skyrmionic Tube In Free Space
authors: Sicong Wang, Zhikai Zhou, Yongjie Zhu, Jialin Sun, Jiahui Mao, Minghui Wang, Shichao Song, Zi-Lan Deng, Yaoyu Cao, Fei Qin, Yunkun Wu, Xifeng Ren, And Xiangping Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sicong Wang, Zhikai Zhou, Yongjie Zhu, Jialin Sun, Jiahui Mao, Minghui Wang, Shichao Song, Zi-lan Deng, Yaoyu Cao, Fei Qin, Yunkun Wu, Xifeng Ren, and Xiangping Li

Optical skyrmions are topological textures of electromagnetic fields with promising applications in information processing, transport, and storage. Exquisitely tailoring the optical fields of diverse physical quantities has expanded the family of skyrmions, yet such skyrmions only exhibit a single-q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223803] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of an optical skyrmionic tube with dual spin and Poynting vector textures in free space.
motivation: Optical skyrmions are topological textures promising for information processing, but previous realizations only exhibited a single type of texture. The authors aim to create a skyrmionic tube with both spin and Poynting vector textures.
method: They use a tightly focused radially polarized beam with a superimposed optical vortex to generate a three-dimensional skyrmionic tube structure, and measure the spin and Poynting vector distributions via near-field imaging.
result: They observe a skyrmionic tube with a spin texture forming a Néel-type skyrmion and a Poynting vector texture forming an anti-skyrmion, coexisting in the same structure.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new type of optical skyrmion with dual textures, which may enable advanced information encoding and manipulation using structured light.

title: Benchmark Calculations Of Charge State Distributions And Radiative Properties Of Gold Plasmas In Icf Hohlraums
authors: Yongjun Li, Cheng Gao, Yong Hou, Fengtao Jin, Jiaolong Zeng, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Yongjun Li, Cheng Gao, Yong Hou, Fengtao Jin, Jiaolong Zeng, and Jianmin Yuan

Accurate ionization balance of gold plasmas in nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium is essential for understanding the physics involved in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) hohlraums, where the persistent “drive deficit” issue may stem from an overestimation of the emission and absorption opacity of g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 225101] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents benchmark calculations of charge state distributions and radiative properties of gold plasmas in ICF hohlraums, focusing on non-LTE ionization balance and opacity.
motivation: Accurate ionization balance of gold plasmas is essential for understanding the 'drive deficit' issue in inertial confinement fusion hohlraums, which may stem from overestimated emission and absorption opacity.

result: The paper provides benchmark charge state distributions and radiative properties that can be used to improve opacity models for ICF simulations.
conclusion: The results help address the drive deficit problem by providing more accurate opacity data for gold plasmas in ICF hohlraums.

title: $n=8$ Shell Breaking In $^{12}\mathrm{Be}$ From A Single-Particle Perspective
authors: J. Chen et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): J. Chen et al. (ISOLDE Collaboration)

Experimental observations of the low-lying states in [MATH] and their accurate modeling play an essential role in understanding the disappearance of the [MATH] magic number. Long-standing experimental ambiguities have been clarified using an one-neutron adding ([MATH], [MATH]) reaction on $^{11…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 222501] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nuclear shell breaking in 12Be using a single-particle reaction, which is a topic in nuclear physics.
motivation: To understand the disappearance of the N=8 magic number in 12Be, which is a key question in nuclear structure.

title: Electron Affinity Of The Carbon Dimer From Threshold Photodetachment Spectroscopy
authors: Sruthi Purushu Melath, Michael Hauck, Christine Lochmann, Robert Wild, Timothy P. Softley, Katrin Dulitz, And Roland Wester
abstract:

tldr: This paper measures the electron affinity of the carbon dimer using threshold photodetachment spectroscopy of trapped anions.

title: Mie Scattering Analog Circuit Emulator
authors: Emanuele Corsaro, Marco Balato, Giovanni Miano, Carlo Petrarca, Andrea Alù, And Carlo Forestiere
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Corsaro, Marco Balato, Giovanni Miano, Carlo Petrarca, Andrea Alù, and Carlo Forestiere

Mie scattering describes the linear interaction of electromagnetic waves with spheres of arbitrary composition and size. Here, we introduce and experimentally validate an analog circuit emulator of Mie scattering by temporally dispersive spheres. The emulator reconstructs the full scattering respons…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223802] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analog circuit emulator for Mie scattering, a classical electromagnetic phenomenon.
motivation: To provide a scalable and reconfigurable platform for studying Mie scattering without full-wave simulations.
method: The authors design and experimentally validate an analog circuit that emulates the temporal dispersion and scattering response of a sphere.
result: The circuit accurately reproduces the scattering behavior of dispersive spheres, as demonstrated by experimental measurements.
conclusion: Analog circuit emulation offers a practical tool for exploring Mie scattering dynamics, with potential applications in metamaterials and photonics.

In conventional quadratic nonlinear interactions with femtosecond lasers, group-velocity mismatch (GVM) is typically regarded as a detrimental effect that restricts the phase-matching bandwidth. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063509] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a counterintuitive ultrafast parametric process where group-velocity mismatch actively facilitates broadband phase-matching in quadratic nonlinear interactions.
motivation: Conventional wisdom treats group-velocity mismatch as detrimental to phase-matching bandwidth in femtosecond parametric processes. The authors aim to show that nonvanished GVMs can be harnessed to achieve ultrafast parametric interactions without requiring broadband phase-matching.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate a parametric process where GVMs are not compensated but instead used to enable efficient nonlinear interactions over a broad bandwidth.

title: Affine Transformations For Purely Anisotropic Cloaking In Flexural Elastic Thin Plates
authors: Léo Pradier, Baptiste Chomette, Manuel Collet, Grégoire Pizon, Morvan Ouisse, Valentin Rapine, And Arnaud Hubert

motivation: Bending wave cloaking in thin plates is a longstanding challenge due to dispersive guided waves; the authors aim to provide a manufacturable design methodology.
method: The approach uses affine transformations to design a unidirectional cloaking structure and validates it numerically and experimentally with composite materials.
result: Broadband cloaking performance is demonstrated through both simulations and experiments.
conclusion: The proposed framework enables practical implementation of elastic wave cloaking in thin plates.

title: Innate Behavioral Mechanisms And Defensive Traits In Ecological Models Of Predator-prey Types
authors: Sangeeta Saha, Swadesh Pal, And Roderick Melnik

result: The model shows that inducible defenses and mutual interference can lead to complex dynamics such as limit cycles and bistability.
conclusion: Inducible defenses and predator interference are key factors in shaping predator-prey interactions and ecosystem stability.

title: Zonal Magnetic Fields Regulate Nonlinear Edge-localized-mode Dynamics Via Self-consistent Force Balance

motivation: Edge-localized modes threaten fusion reactor components, so understanding their nonlinear dynamics is crucial for reactor design.
method: Nonlinear full-torus MHD simulations are used to model the effect of turbulence-driven zonal magnetic fields on ELM evolution.
result: Zonal magnetic fields regulate ELM dynamics through self-consistent force balance, affecting heat and particle bursts.
conclusion: Zonal magnetic fields play an essential role in nonlinear ELM evolution and should be considered in fusion plasma control.

title: Electron Penetration Heating In Turbulent Magnetic Loops Driven By Nonrelativistic Laser-plasma Interaction
authors: Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, And Matthew R. Edwards

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065205] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron penetration heating in turbulent magnetic loops driven by nonrelativistic laser-plasma interaction using particle-in-cell simulations.

method: Particle-in-cell simulations of nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in under-critical plasma.
result: Identified electron penetration heating during growth of turbulent magnetic loops with left-hand chirality.

title: Effects Of Hydrodynamic Motion On The Stopping Power And Energy Deposition Of Alpha Particles In An Inertial Confinement Fusion Hotspot

result: Hydrodynamic motion reduces the stopping power and energy deposition of alpha particles, affecting hotspot ignition conditions.

result: Natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and promoted apoptosis, but only scouted around fibroblasts without forming aggregates.
conclusion: The response is specific to cancer cells, suggesting potential for targeted immunotherapy, but further tests with other cell types are needed.

conclusion: Multiobjective tweezers enable complex manipulation tasks in scattering media, with potential applications in acoustofluidics and biomedical engineering.

In a recent paper, Chyba et al. [
tldr: This comment refutes a claim of generating electric power from Earth's rotation using a stationary device, showing it violates fundamental physics.

tldr: This paper presents a novel method for longitudinally resolved measurement of energy-transfer efficiency in a plasma-wakefield accelerator.
motivation: Conventional efficiency measurements are invasive and provide only averaged values; a non-invasive, resolved method is needed for better understanding and optimization.
method: The authors use a longitudinally resolved diagnostic technique based on coherent transition radiation to measure the energy-transfer efficiency along the plasma wakefield.
result: They demonstrate the ability to measure efficiency with high spatial resolution, revealing variations along the accelerator that were previously averaged out.
conclusion: The technique enables detailed study of energy transfer dynamics, which is crucial for improving the performance of plasma-wakefield accelerators.

title: Long-range Topotaxis As A Result Of Supercellular Topographic Anisotropy During Chemotaxis

Highly motile cells, like patrolling leukocytes during immune response and amoeboid sarcoma cells during metastasis, navigate relatively long distances in complex environments where they encounter a wide variety of topographic structures on different length scales. Subcellular topographic substrate …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023234] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how cells navigate long distances using topographic anisotropy during chemotaxis, a topic in biophysics and cell motility.
motivation: Understanding how highly motile cells like leukocytes and sarcoma cells navigate complex environments with varying topographic structures is crucial for immune response and metastasis.
method: The authors model cell migration as a stochastic process on a substrate with supercellular topographic anisotropy, analyzing the resulting long-range topotaxis.
result: They find that topographic anisotropy can guide cells over long distances, complementing chemotactic cues.
conclusion: Topographic features of the environment play a significant role in long-range cell navigation, which has implications for immune response and cancer metastasis.

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.

tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications, breaking the traditional bandwidth limit.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A unified model emerges where tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdown.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more reliable high-power technologies and advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: To understand strong interaction (QCD) through charmonium decays and search for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights BESIII's leading role in high-precision measurements.
conclusion: Hadron production in open-charm meson pairs provides crucial insights into QCD and quark confinement.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of planetary radar observations at Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To summarize the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system after its upgrade.
method: Review of radar techniques and key observations of planets, moons, and asteroids.
result: Highlights Arecibo's unique contributions to planetary science, including surface and subsurface characterization.
conclusion: Arecibo radar was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary exploration, now lost.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, optical, and satellite instruments.
result: Highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory provided unique capabilities for geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform current studies.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and their detection could provide insights into dense matter physics.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects with future gravitational-wave detectors and discusses connections to electromagnetic observations.
result: It outlines the potential for multimessenger observations to inform nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves is a promising but challenging field that will benefit from next-generation detectors.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the precipitation bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in ground-based interferometers.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare multimessenger events; detecting gravitational waves would provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes latest progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents an overview of predicted gravitational wave signatures and the status of detection strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave observations from a Galactic supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, but the paper does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties constrain the behavior of matter at extreme densities.
method: The review summarizes recent measurements from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile observations, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements provide constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, challenging the cosmological principle.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole in galaxy/quasar catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in their distribution, and comparison with the CMB dipole interpreted as due to our peculiar motion.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further work is needed to rule out systematic biases.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on galaxy and large-scale structure formation.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test beyond-standard-model physics through astrophysical observations.
method: The paper is a review summarizing theoretical predictions of self-interacting dark matter and comparing them with observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: It provides an overview of current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and discusses future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, and upcoming surveys will further constrain its properties.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers new discovery potential.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have been placed on supersymmetric parameter space, narrowing viable models.
conclusion: The HL-LHC may discover supersymmetry if it exists in certain well-motivated scenarios, but no new results are presented.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and their astrophysical implications.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and atomic effects in the solar interior.
result: Updated reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic observations.
conclusion: The new data and theory refine our understanding of solar fusion, but the paper is purely astrophysical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Gas bubbles are ubiquitous in natural and industrial processes, and understanding their dynamics is crucial for modeling two-phase flows.
method: The paper reviews key advances over the past 20 years, focusing on experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, deformation, and interactions.
result: Highlights the effects of added mass, deformable surfaces, turbulence, rheology, and surfactants on bubble dynamics.
conclusion: Provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth is important for materials science and biology.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and the nonlinear phenomena accompanying buckling.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal conditions in the first second after the Big Bang, which are opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave sources (phase transitions, topological defects) and detection strategies.
result: Summarizes potential signals and detection methods for stochastic gravitational waves from early universe events.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of the early universe, but detection requires future experiments.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the origin and stability of isolated potential humps observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by standard quasineutral plasma theory.
method: Review of satellite observations, laboratory experiments, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetically unstable velocity distributions and can be stable over long timescales.
conclusion: Kinetic effects are essential for explaining these structures, and further study is needed to fully understand their role in plasma dynamics.
